Calculate the volume in cm³ of oxygen evolved at s.t.p when a current of 5 A is passed through acidified water for 193 s. 

[F = 96500 C mol⁻¹. Molar volume of a gas at s.t.p = 22.4 dm³]
questions.explanation: Charge = I × t = 5 × 193 = 965 C. Moles of electrons = 965/96500 = 0.01 mol. At the anode: 2H₂O → O₂ + 4H⁺ + 4e⁻, so moles of O₂ = 0.01/4 = 0.0025 mol. Volume of O₂ = 0.0025 × 22.4 = 0.056 dm³.

questions.text: A liquid that will dissolve fast is
Aluminium hydroxide is used in the dyeing industry as a
questions.explanation: Al(OH)₃ is used as a mordant in the dyeing industry. A mordant is a substance that fixes dye to fabric by forming an insoluble complex (lake) with the dye molecules, helping the colour adhere permanently to the textile fibres.

questions.text: The ores that can be concentrated by flotation are
A charge in the temperature of a saturated solution disturbs the equilibrium between the
options: Dissolved solute and the undissolved solute

questions.text: One of the following is not a water pollutant?
questions.explanation: Oxygen gas (O₂) is not a water pollutant. In fact, dissolved oxygen is essential for the survival of aquatic organisms. Inorganic fertilizers cause eutrophication, warm water effluent (thermal pollution) reduces dissolved oxygen levels and harms aquatic life, and biodegradable waste depletes oxygen as it decomposes. None of these are beneficial to water quality, whereas oxygen is necessary.

questions.text: A noble gas with a high power of fog penetration used in aerodrome beacons is
2CO + O₂ → 2CO₂. Calculate the volume of the resulting mixture at the end of the reaction, if 50 cm³ of carbon (II) oxide was exploded in 100 cm³ of oxygen.
questions.explanation: From the equation 2CO + O₂ → 2CO₂, ratio CO:O₂:CO₂ = 2:1:2. 50 cm³ CO reacts with 50/2 = 25 cm³ O₂ to produce 50 cm³ CO₂. Excess O₂ remaining = 100 - 25 = 75 cm³. Total volume of mixture = CO₂ + excess O₂ = 50 + 75 = 125 cm³.

questions.text: Alloys are best prepared by
options: reducing and mixture of their metallic
cooking a molten of the metals
questions.explanation: Alloys are best prepared by melting (fusing) the component metals together in the molten state and allowing the mixture to cool and solidify. This ensures homogeneous mixing of the metals at the atomic level, producing a uniform alloy.

questions.text: How many moles of CO₂ are produced when ethanol is burnt with 6g of oxygen?
questions.explanation: Equation: C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O. Moles of O₂ = 6 ÷ 32 = 0.1875 mol. From equation, 3 mol O₂ produces 2 mol CO₂. Moles of CO₂ = (2/3) × 0.1875 = 0.125 mol.

questions.text: The gas that is commonly used to demonstrate the fountain experiment is
questions.explanation: Hydrogen chloride (HCl) is extremely soluble in water (about 500 volumes per volume of water). When a flask of HCl is inverted over water, rapid dissolution creates a near-vacuum, drawing water up in a dramatic fountain. This high solubility makes HCl the classic gas for the fountain experiment.

questions.text: In the diagram, X is
questions.explanation: The apparatus shows the laboratory preparation of SO₂: a liquid (likely concentrated H₂SO₄) in the round-bottom flask reacting with a solid (e.g., copper or sodium sulphite) in the conical flask Y, generating a gas collected at X. The gas produced in this setup is SO₂ (sulphur dioxide). SO₃ requires industrial catalytic conditions; H₂S would require different reagents (e.g., FeS + HCl).

questions.text: The colour of methyl orange in alkaline medium is
Natural water collected from rivers and ponds contains oxygen, carbon(IV) oxide and
Hydrogen can be displaced from a hot alkaline solution by
questions.explanation: Calcium (Ca) is reactive enough to displace hydrogen from a hot alkaline solution. It reacts vigorously with water/alkaline solutions: Ca + 2H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + H₂↑. Cu and Fe are insufficiently reactive, while Sn only reacts with strong acids.

questions.text: 127g of sodium chloride was dissolved in 1.0dm³ of distilled water at 25°C. Determine the solubility in moldm⁻³ of sodium chloride at that temperature. [Na = 23, Cl = 35.5]
questions.explanation: Molar mass of NaCl = 23 + 35.5 = 58.5 g/mol. Moles of NaCl = 127 ÷ 58.5 = 2.17 mol. Volume = 1.0 dm³. Solubility = 2.17 ÷ 1.0 = 2.17 mol/dm³ ≈ 2.2 mol/dm³.

questions.text: The nucleus of a hydrogen atom consists of a?
questions.explanation: The most common isotope of hydrogen (protium, ¹H) has an atomic number of 1, meaning its nucleus contains exactly 1 proton and no neutrons. The single electron orbits outside the nucleus. Deuterium (²H) has 1 proton and 1 neutron, and tritium (³H) has 1 proton and 2 neutrons, but the ordinary hydrogen atom nucleus contains only 1 proton.

questions.text: Beryllium and Aluminium have similar properties because they
options: are positioned diagonally to each other
questions.explanation: Beryllium (Be, Group 2, Period 2) and Aluminium (Al, Group 13, Period 3) exhibit similar chemical properties due to the diagonal relationship in the periodic table. Elements diagonally adjacent show similarities because the increase in period number (↓) and group number (→) have opposing effects on properties, resulting in nearly identical charge density and electronegativity.

questions.text: An organic compound contains 53.1% Carbon, 6.2% Hydrogen, 12.4% Nitrogen, and 28.3% Oxygen by mass. What is the molecular formula of the compound if its vapour density is 56.5? [C=12, H=1, N=14, O=16]
questions.explanation: Mole ratio: C = 53.1/12 = 4.425; H = 6.2/1 = 6.2; N = 12.4/14 = 0.886; O = 28.3/16 = 1.769. Divide by smallest (0.886): C = 5.0; H = 7.0; N = 1.0; O = 2.0. Empirical formula = C₅H₇NO₂. Empirical formula mass = 60+7+14+32 = 113. Molar mass = 2 × vapour density = 2 × 56.5 = 113 g/mol. n = 113 ÷ 113 = 1. Molecular formula = C₅H₇NO₂.

questions.text: The pollutant usually present in a city which generates its electricity from coal?
questions.explanation: Coal contains significant amounts of sulphur. When coal is burned to generate electricity, sulphur is oxidised to sulphur(IV) oxide (SO₂). SO₂ is the primary pollutant associated with coal-burning power stations. It causes acid rain and respiratory problems. Smog results from photochemical reactions, and CO is produced from incomplete combustion rather than coal-burning power stations specifically.

questions.text: Vulcanization involve the removal of
questions.explanation: Vulcanization involves the removal (or breaking) of carbon-carbon double bonds in rubber molecules. Sulfur reacts with these double bonds to create cross-links between polymer chains, converting soft rubber into harder, more durable material.

questions.text: The number of electrons in the valence shell of an element of atomic number 14 is
questions.explanation: Element with atomic number 14 is Silicon (Si). Its electronic configuration is 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p². The valence shell is the third shell (n=3), which contains 3s²3p² = 2 + 2 = 4 electrons. Silicon therefore has 4 valence electrons.

questions.text: Four elements P, Q, R and S have atomic numbers of 4, 10, 12 and 14 respectively. Which of these elements is a noble gas?
questions.explanation: Atomic number 10 is neon (Ne), which belongs to Group 18 (noble gases). Its configuration is 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ — a completely filled outer shell. Atomic number 4 is beryllium, 12 is magnesium, and 14 is silicon — none of these are noble gases.

questions.text: The relative atomic mass of a naturally occurring lithium consisting of 90% ⁷₃Li and 10% ⁶₃Li is
Elements in the periodic table are arranged in the order of their
questions.explanation: The modern periodic table arranges elements in order of increasing atomic number (number of protons). This arrangement was established by Moseley and corrected limitations of Mendeleev's table, which used relative atomic mass and led to inconsistencies with elements like argon and potassium.

questions.text: Which of the following equimolar solutions will have the highest pH
Alloys are best prepared by
options: Reducing a mixture of their metallic oxides
Cooling a molten mixture of the metals

questions.text: Phosphorous is stored under water to precvent it from
Stainless steel is an alloy made up of?
questions.explanation: Stainless steel is an alloy composed primarily of iron and chromium, typically containing at least 10.5% chromium by mass. The chromium forms a thin, invisible oxide layer on the surface that prevents corrosion and staining. Nickel is often also added. Copper and tin form bronze, iron and carbon form ordinary steel, and iron and zinc form galvanised iron.

questions.text: The oxidation state of chlorine in HClO4 is
What are the possible oxidation numbers of an element if its atomic number is 17?
questions.explanation: Atomic number 17 is chlorine, with electron configuration [Ne] 3s² 3p⁵ — 7 valence electrons. Chlorine can gain 1 electron to achieve −1 oxidation state, or lose electrons to reach +1, +3, +5, or +7. The extreme oxidation states are −1 and +7.

questions.text: A difference between chemical and physical change is that in a chemical change
questions.explanation: The defining characteristic of a chemical change is that a new substance with different chemical properties is formed. Physical changes alter the form or state of matter without producing a new substance. Options A, B, and C can occur in both types of change.

questions.text: What happens to the position of equilibrium, if a reversible exothermic reaction is subjected to a decrease in temperature?
options: The position of equilibrium shifts to the left
The position of equilibrium shifts to the right.
The position of equilibrium remains unchanged
questions.explanation: For a reversible exothermic reaction, the forward reaction releases heat. By Le Chatelier's principle, decreasing temperature removes heat from the system. The equilibrium shifts in the direction that produces more heat, which is the forward (exothermic) direction. The equilibrium position therefore shifts to the right, increasing the yield of products.

questions.text: P(g) + O(g)    ⇌ 3R(s)  +  S(g)   ΔH is negative which of the following will increase the yield of R
The enzyme used in the hydrolysis of starch to dextrin and maltose is
questions.explanation: Amylase catalyses the hydrolysis of starch, breaking the glycosidic bonds to produce dextrin (intermediate) and then maltose. Salivary and pancreatic amylase perform this function in digestion. Lipase digests fats; invertase hydrolyses sucrose; zymase converts sugars to ethanol.

questions.text: Which of these reagents can confirm the presence of a triple bond
A sample of any of the following substances disappears after some time when exposed to air like camphor, naphthalene, or dry ice. This phenomenon is called?
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the direct conversion of a solid into vapour without passing through the liquid state. Camphor, naphthalene, and dry ice (solid CO₂) all sublime at room conditions, gradually disappearing as they convert directly from solid to gas. Evaporation applies to liquids, not solids.

questions.text: When chlorine is passed into water and the resulting solution exposed to sunlight, the product formed are
The ion that can be used as an oxidizing agent is
When salt loses its water of crystallization to the atmosphere on exposure, the process is said to be
questions.explanation: When a salt loses its water of crystallization to the atmosphere on exposure, the process is efflorescence. The hydrated crystals spontaneously lose water and become powdery.

questions.text: Which of the following substances is a mixture?
questions.explanation: A mixture contains two or more substances not chemically combined. Seawater is a mixture of water, dissolved salts (NaCl, MgCl₂, etc.), and other substances in variable proportions. Granulated sugar (sucrose), sodium chloride, and iron are all pure substances with fixed compositions.

questions.text: Which of the following organic compounds is very soluble in water
Transition metals posses variable oxidation states because they have
options: A variable number of electrons in the p orbitals

questions.text: The produce of the combustion of candle wax are
n monosaccharide ⇌ (P/Q) polysaccharide + n water. In the process above, P and Q respectively represent
questions.explanation: In the forward direction (monosaccharides → polysaccharide + water), water is eliminated — this is condensation polymerization. In the reverse direction (polysaccharide + water → monosaccharides), the polymer is broken down by water — this is hydrolysis. Therefore P = condensation and Q = hydrolysis.

questions.text: The furring of kettles is caused by the presence of what compound in water?
questions.explanation: Furring (scale/limescale) in kettles is caused by calcium hydrogentrioxocarbonate (IV), Ca(HCO₃)₂, present in temporary hard water. On heating, it decomposes: Ca(HCO₃)₂ → CaCO₃↓ + H₂O + CO₂, depositing insoluble calcium trioxocarbonate as scale.

questions.text: The salt formed from a weak acid and a strong base hydrolyzes in water to form
questions.explanation: A salt formed from a weak acid and a strong base (e.g., CH₃COONa from acetic acid + NaOH) undergoes hydrolysis in water. The anion of the weak acid accepts a proton from water, producing OH⁻ ions. This makes the solution alkaline (pH > 7).

questions.text: The solubility of a salt of molar mass 101g at 200C is 0.34mol dm-3. If 3.40g of the salt is dissolved completely in 250cm3 of water in a beaker, the resulting solution is
IN which of the following is the oxidation number of sulphur equal to -2
The pH of a 0.001 mol dm⁻³ of H₂SO₄ is [Log₁₀2 = 0.3]
questions.explanation: H₂SO₄ is a diprotic strong acid: H₂SO₄ → 2H⁺ + SO₄²⁻. [H⁺] = 2 × 0.001 = 0.002 mol/dm³. pH = −log(0.002) = −log(2 × 10⁻³) = −(log 2 + log 10⁻³) = −(0.3 − 3) = −(−2.7) = 2.7.

questions.text: Nitrogen, a component of air is used for
questions.explanation: Nitrogen from air is used to produce ammonia (NH₃) via the Haber process, which is then oxidized to nitric acid (HNO₃) via the Ostwald process. Margarine production uses hydrogen, and cooling agents use other gases.

questions.text: An aqueous solution of a metal salt M gives a white precipitate with NaOH which dissolves in excess NaOH. With aqueous ammonia, the solution of M also gives a white precipitate which dissolves in excess ammonia. Therefore the cation in M is
questions.explanation: Zn²⁺ gives a white precipitate of Zn(OH)₂ with NaOH, which dissolves in excess NaOH (amphoteric): Zn(OH)₂ + 2OH⁻ → [Zn(OH)₄]²⁻. It also gives a white precipitate with NH₃ solution that dissolves in excess NH₃ to form the tetraamminezinc complex: Zn(OH)₂ + 4NH₃ → [Zn(NH₃)₄]²⁺. Al³⁺ dissolves in excess NaOH but not in excess NH₃, eliminating option C.

questions.text: The pair of organic compounds that are isomers is
Which of the noble gases has the greatest ionization energy
questions.explanation: Helium has the greatest ionization energy among noble gases because it has the smallest atomic radius and strongest nuclear attraction on its electrons.

questions.text: Which of these is the most preferred separation technique for the isolation of solutes where the purity of the constituent is of utmost importance?
questions.explanation: Recrystallization is the preferred technique when purity is of utmost importance. The solute is dissolved in a hot solvent, then allowed to cool slowly. Pure crystals form as the solubility decreases, leaving impurities behind in solution. The crystals are then filtered off, yielding a highly pure product. Distillation separates liquids, sieving separates by particle size, and precipitation does not yield the same level of purity.

questions.text: A characteristic of the alkane family is
Tin is unaffected by air at ordinary temperature due to its
questions.explanation: Tin is resistant to corrosion at ordinary temperatures because of its weak electropositive (low reactivity) character. It has a low tendency to lose electrons and oxidize in air. This weak electropositive character means it does not readily react with oxygen or moisture at room temperature, making it useful as a protective coating (tinning).

questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct about the average kinetic energy of the molecules of a gas
options: It inctreasaes with increase in pressure
It increases with increase in temperature

The process by which atoms are rearranged into different molecular structures in the petroleum refining process is referred to as
Neutral atoms of neon with atomic number 10 have the same number of electrons as
The sulphide which is insoluble in dilute hydrochloric acid is
questions.explanation: CuS (copper II sulphide) is insoluble in dilute HCl because it is an extremely insoluble sulphide with a very low Ksp. FeS, ZnS, and Na₂S all dissolve in dilute HCl to produce H₂S gas. CuS requires hot concentrated HNO₃ or aqua regia to dissolve.

questions.text: The compound that is used as an anaesthetic is

Cu₂S(s) + O₂(g) = 2Cu(s) + SO₂(g). 

In the above reaction, the oxidation number of Cu changes from ___ to ___?
questions.explanation: In Cu₂S, copper has oxidation number +1 (since S is -2 and there are 2 Cu atoms: 2x + (-2) = 0, x = +1). In the product Cu(s), copper is in its elemental state with oxidation number 0. Therefore Cu changes from +1 to 0 (reduction).

questions.text: A compound contains 40.0% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen and 53.3% oxygen. If the molar mass of the compound is 180. Find the molecular formula. [H = 1, C = 12, O = 16]
questions.explanation: Mole ratio — C: 40.0/12 = 3.33; H: 6.7/1 = 6.7; O: 53.3/16 = 3.33. Divide by smallest (3.33): C:H:O = 1:2:1. Empirical formula = CH₂O. Empirical formula mass = 12 + 2 + 16 = 30. n = 180 ÷ 30 = 6. Molecular formula = C₆H₁₂O₆.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about catalyst is false?
options: catalysts do not appear in the balanced equation
catalysts reduce the activation energy for a reaction
catalysts do not alter the mechanism of the reaction and never appear in the rate law
questions.explanation: Option D is false. Catalysts DO alter the mechanism of the reaction — they provide an alternative pathway with lower activation energy. They also CAN appear in the rate law (rate equation), especially homogeneous catalysts whose concentration affects the rate. Options A, B, and C are all true statements about catalysts.

questions.text: When chlorine water is exposed to bright sunlight, the following products are formed
questions.explanation: Chlorine water contains Cl₂, HCl, and HOCl in equilibrium: Cl₂ + H₂O ⇌ HCl + HOCl. On exposure to bright sunlight, the HOCl decomposes: 2HOCl → 2HCl + O₂. The overall result is the production of HCl(aq) and O₂. This is why chlorine water bleaches more rapidly in sunlight.

questions.text: The scientist who stated that matter can be converted into energy is?
questions.explanation: Albert Einstein proposed the mass-energy equivalence through his famous equation E = mc², which states that matter (mass) can be converted into energy and vice versa. Boyle formulated the gas law relating pressure and volume, Lavoisier established the law of conservation of mass, and Avogadro proposed his hypothesis about equal volumes of gases.

questions.text: What mass of magnesium would be obtained by passing a current of 2 amperes for 2 hours 30 mins, through molten magnesium chloride? [1 faraday = 96500C, Mg = 24]
questions.explanation: Time = 2 hrs 30 min = 9000 s. Charge = 2 × 9000 = 18000 C. Mg²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Mg, so 2 Faradays deposit 24 g of Mg. Faradays used = 18000 ÷ 96500 = 0.1865 F. Mass of Mg = (0.1865 ÷ 2) × 24 = 2.24 g.

questions.text: The maximum number of electrons in the L shell of an atom is
Which of the following gives a precipitation when treated with NaOH solution?
questions.explanation: AlCl₃ reacts with NaOH to form aluminium hydroxide, Al(OH)₃, a white gelatinous precipitate: AlCl₃ + 3NaOH → Al(OH)₃↓ + 3NaCl. NH₄Cl produces ammonia gas (not a precipitate), while Na₂CO₃ and CH₃COONa are fully soluble in NaOH.

questions.text: The elements that belong to the third period of periodic table are
questions.explanation: The third period (Period 3) contains elements with atomic numbers 11–18: Na, Mg, Al, Si, P, S, Cl, and Ar. Option D (Na, Mg, S, Ar) are all correctly in Period 3. The other options contain Period 2 elements (Li, Be, B, C, N, O).

questions.text: H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O. The equation above illustrates?
questions.explanation: The equation H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O represents the ionic equation for neutralization, which is the reaction between an acid (providing H⁺) and a base (providing OH⁻) to form water. This is the net ionic equation for all strong acid-strong base neutralization reactions.

questions.text: Cancerous growths are cured by exposure to
If 1 litre of 2.2 M sulphuric acid is poured into a bucket containing 10 litres of water and the resulting solution mixed thoroughly, the resulting sulphuric acid concentration will be
questions.explanation: Using C₁V₁ = C₂V₂. C₁ = 2.2 M, V₁ = 1 L, V₂ = 1 + 10 = 11 L. C₂ = (2.2 × 1)/11 = 0.20 M.

questions.text: When Sulphur(IV)oxide is passed into solution of acidified tetraoxomanganate(VII), the colour changes from
questions.explanation: Acidified potassium tetraoxomanganate(VII) (KMnO₄) is purple in colour. SO₂ acts as a reducing agent, reducing the purple MnO₄⁻ ions (Mn oxidation state +7) to colourless Mn²⁺ ions (oxidation state +2). The SO₂ is simultaneously oxidised to SO₄²⁻. The purple colour of the KMnO₄ solution is therefore discharged, turning the solution colourless.

questions.text: Proteins in acid solution undergo?
questions.explanation: Proteins are polymers of amino acids linked by peptide bonds. In acid solution, water molecules break these peptide bonds in a reaction called hydrolysis, producing the constituent amino acids. This is the reverse of condensation polymerisation and is used in protein digestion and laboratory analysis.

questions.text: What is the sum of the oxidation numbers in a neutral compound?
questions.explanation: In a neutral compound, the sum of the oxidation numbers of all atoms must equal zero. This is a fundamental rule of oxidation number assignment. For example, in H₂O: 2(+1) + (−2) = 0. In CO₂: (+4) + 2(−2) = 0. The algebraic sum is always zero for electrically neutral compounds.

questions.text: A binary compound of oxygen with another element is referred to as?
questions.explanation: An oxide is a binary compound formed between oxygen and another element. Binary means it contains exactly two different elements, one of which is oxygen. Examples include water (H₂O), iron oxide (Fe₂O₃), carbon dioxide (CO₂), and sodium oxide (Na₂O). All these are classified as oxides.

questions.text: N₂O₄ ⇌ 2NO₂ (Δ = -ve). From the reaction above, which of these conditions would produce the highest equilibrium yield for N₂O₄?
questions.explanation: The forward reaction (N₂O₄ formation) is exothermic (ΔH = −ve). By Le Chatelier's principle: (1) Low temperature favours the exothermic forward reaction, increasing N₂O₄ yield. (2) The forward reaction also involves 2 moles of gas converting to 1 mole — a decrease in moles. High pressure favours the side with fewer moles of gas, which is the forward reaction (N₂O₄ side). Therefore, low temperature and high pressure give the highest yield of N₂O₄.

questions.text: All these are electromagnetic waves except
questions.explanation: A photon is a quantum (particle) of electromagnetic energy, not a type of electromagnetic wave. White light, X-rays, and infrared radiation are all types of electromagnetic waves within the electromagnetic spectrum.

questions.text: What is the trend for ionization energy across a period in the periodic table?
questions.explanation: Across a period from left to right, the atomic number increases, meaning more protons are added to the nucleus. This increases the nuclear charge, which attracts electrons more strongly. As a result, more energy is required to remove an electron, so ionization energy increases from left to right across a period.

questions.text: An example of an alkaline gas is
questions.explanation: NH₃ (ammonia) dissolves in water to form an alkaline solution (NH₄OH). HCl forms an acidic solution, NO₂ forms acidic solutions, and N₂ is neutral. NH₃ is the only alkaline gas listed.

questions.text: Which of the following is the best starting material for the preparation of oxygen by heating trioxonitrate (V) with?
questions.explanation: Lead (II) trioxonitrate (V) [Pb(NO₃)₂] on heating decomposes to give oxygen most readily: 2Pb(NO₃)₂ → 2PbO + 4NO₂ + O₂. It is the best starting material because the reaction is clean and produces O₂ at moderate temperatures. NaNO₃ gives NaNO₂ + O₂ but requires higher temperatures; Zn and Ca nitrates behave similarly but Pb(NO₃)₂ is the classic lab choice.

questions.text: The ideal gas laws and equations are true for all gases at
questions.explanation: Ideal gas behaviour is most closely approximated at low pressures (gas molecules are far apart, minimizing intermolecular forces) and high temperatures (molecules have high kinetic energy relative to intermolecular attractions). At high pressures or low temperatures, real gas behaviour deviates significantly from ideal.

questions.text: The intermediate product formed when ethanol is progressively oxidized to ethanoic acid with potassium heptaoxodichromate(VI) is
How many valence electrons are contained in the element ³¹₁₅P?
questions.explanation: Phosphorus (atomic number 15) has the electron configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p³. The outermost shell (n=3) contains 2 + 3 = 5 electrons. .

questions.text: The maximum number of electrons in the N shell is?
questions.explanation: The maximum number of electrons in any shell is given by the formula 2n², where n is the principal quantum number. For the N shell, n = 4. Maximum electrons = 2 × 4² = 2 × 16 = 32.

questions.text: A compound gives an orange red colour to a non luminous flame. This compound is likely to contain
When 5.0cm3 of a saturated solution of sugar of molar mass 342g at 400C was evaporated to dryness, 34.2g of dry solid was obtained. The solubility of sugar at 400C is
A consequence of global warming is
Silver and Gold are metals found as free uncombined elements in the earth's crust, which makes them to be referred to as
questions.explanation: Silver and gold are called noble metals because they occur naturally in the free (uncombined) elemental state in the earth's crust. They are unreactive and resist corrosion and oxidation. The term "noble" reflects their low chemical reactivity and their position at the bottom of the electrochemical/reactivity series.

questions.text: What volume (dm³) of water will be added to 10dm³ of 2.0 mol/dm³ HCl acid solution to give a final solution of 0.5 mol/dm³?
questions.explanation: Using the dilution formula: C₁V₁ = C₂V₂. C₁ = 2.0 mol/dm³; V₁ = 10 dm³; C₂ = 0.5 mol/dm³. V₂ = (2.0 × 10) ÷ 0.5 = 40 dm³. Volume of water added = V₂ − V₁ = 40 − 10 = 30 dm³.

questions.text: The diagram represents
questions.explanation: In the diagram, the reactants are at a higher potential energy level than the products, meaning energy is released during the reaction. This is the profile of an exothermic reaction (ΔH < 0). The activated complex at the peak represents the transition state. An endothermic reaction would show products at a higher energy level than reactants.

questions.text: Carbohydrates can generally be represented by the general formula Cₓ(H₂O)ᵧ. For fructose the value of x is
questions.explanation: Fructose has the molecular formula C₆H₁₂O₆. Written in the form Cₓ(H₂O)ᵧ: C₆(H₂O)₆, so x = 6 and y = 6. The value of x is 6.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is false about hard water?
options: Helps animals to build strong teeth
Cannot be supplied in pipes made of lead
Helps animals to build strong bones
questions.explanation: Hard water contains dissolved Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions which help build strong bones and teeth (A and D are true), and it does taste better than soft water (C is true). Statement B is false: hard water can be supplied in lead pipes because it deposits a protective scale of calcium carbonate inside the pipes, preventing lead from dissolving. It is soft water that is dangerous in lead pipes.

questions.text: The oxidation number of iodine in KIO₃ is
questions.explanation: In KIO₃: K = +1, O = -2. Let I = x. +1 + x + 3(-2) = 0 → 1 + x - 6 = 0 → x = +5. The oxidation number of iodine in KIO₃ is +5.

questions.text: Iron produced directly from a blast furnace is
questions.explanation: The iron tapped directly from a blast furnace is called pig iron. It contains about 3-4% carbon and other impurities. Pig iron is then further refined to produce wrought iron, cast iron, or steel.

questions.text: ²²⁶₈₈Ra → ˣ₈₆Rn + alpha particle. What is the value of x?
questions.explanation: In alpha decay, the mass number decreases by 4 and the atomic number decreases by 2. Mass number of Rn = 226 - 4 = 222. Atomic number of Rn = 88 - 2 = 86. Therefore x = 222, giving ²²²₈₆Rn.

questions.text: What volume of 0.5mol dm-3 H2SO4 will exactly neutralize 20cm3 of 0.1 mol dm-3 NaOH solution
A correct electrochemical series can be obtained from Na, Ca, Al, Mg, Zn, Fe, Pb, H, Cu, Hg, Ag, Au by interchanging
questions.explanation: The correct reactivity/electrochemical series order is: Na, Ca, Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Pb, H, Cu, Hg, Ag, Au. In the given series, Al and Mg are swapped (Al appears before Mg, but Mg is more reactive). Interchanging Al and Mg corrects the series.

There will be a large increase in free energy
There will be a large decrease in free energy

Elements X and Y have electronic configurations 1s²2s²2p⁴ and 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p¹ respectively. When they combine, the formula of the compound formed is
questions.explanation: X (1s²2s²2p⁴) is oxygen (6 valence electrons, forms O²⁻). Y (1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p¹) is aluminium (3 valence electrons, forms Al³⁺). To balance charges: 2Al³⁺ + 3O²⁻ → Al₂O₃. In the formula Y₂X₃: Y = Al, X = O, giving Al₂O₃. The formula is Y₂X₃.

questions.text: How many atoms are present in 6.0 g of magnesium? [Mg = 24, Nₐ = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹]
questions.explanation: Moles of Mg = 6.0/24 = 0.25 mol. Number of atoms = 0.25 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 1.505 × 10²³ ≈ 1.51 × 10²³ atoms.

questions.text: The solubility of solids that dissolve in a given solvent with the liberation of heat will
options: increase with an increase in temperature
decrease with an increase in temperature
decrease with a decrease in temperature
not be affected by changes in temperature
questions.explanation: When a solid dissolves with liberation of heat (exothermic dissolution, ΔH < 0), the dissolution process releases energy. By Le Chatelier's principle, increasing temperature shifts the equilibrium to oppose the heat, i.e., toward the undissolved solid. Therefore, the solubility decreases with increasing temperature for exothermic dissolution.

How many neutrons are present in an atom with mass number and atomic number 37 and 17 respectively?
questions.explanation: Number of neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 37 − 17 = 20. The atom described is chlorine-37 (³⁷Cl), which has 17 protons and 20 neutrons in its nucleus.

questions.text: 220g of carbon dioxide contains how many moles?
questions.explanation: Molar mass of CO₂ = 12 + (16 × 2) = 44 g/mol. Moles = mass ÷ molar mass = 220 ÷ 44 = 5 moles.

questions.text: The noble gases owe their inactivity to
Which of the following ions requires the largest quantity of electricity for discharge at an electrode
Alkenes are represented with the general molecular formula
questions.explanation: Alkenes contain one C=C double bond and have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ. CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ is for alkanes, CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ is for alkynes, and CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH is for alkanols.

questions.text: Which of the following gives a precipitate when treated with NaOH solution
The mass of one Avogadro number of helium atoms is?
questions.explanation: One Avogadro number (6.02 × 10²³) of atoms of any element equals one mole of that element, which has a mass equal to the molar mass in grams. The molar mass of helium (He) is 4 g/mol. Therefore, one Avogadro number of helium atoms has a mass of 4.00 grams.

questions.text: Biuret test is a chemical test used for detecting the presence of
questions.explanation: The Biuret test detects the presence of proteins (peptide bonds). When dilute sodium hydroxide and a few drops of copper(II) sulphate solution are added to a protein solution, a purple/violet colour develops. The colour results from the coordination of Cu²⁺ ions with the peptide bonds (–CO–NH–) in the protein chain. No colour change occurs with carbohydrates, amines, or esters.

questions.text: An oxidation state of Cr in K₂Cr₂O₇
questions.explanation: In K₂Cr₂O₇: K is +1, O is -2. Let Cr = x. 2(+1) + 2x + 7(-2) = 0 → 2 + 2x - 14 = 0 → 2x = 12 → x = +6. The oxidation state of Cr is +6.

questions.text: On the basis of the electrochemical series, which of these ions will show the greater tendency to be discharged at the cathode in an electrolytic cell?
questions.explanation: At the cathode, reduction occurs and ions are discharged. Ions lower in the electrochemical series (closer to the bottom/more noble) are discharged preferentially. In the electrochemical series: Cu²⁺ > Fe²⁺ > Sn²⁺ > Zn²⁺ in terms of ease of discharge. Cu²⁺ has the highest reduction potential among the options and is therefore discharged most readily at the cathode.

questions.text: What is the concentration of a solution containing 2 g of NaOH in 100 cm³ of solution? [Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.explanation: Molar mass of NaOH = 23 + 16 + 1 = 40 g mol⁻¹. Moles of NaOH = 2/40 = 0.05 mol. Volume = 100 cm³ = 0.1 dm³. Concentration = 0.05/0.1 = 0.50 mol dm⁻³.

questions.text: The mass number of a nucleus is?
options: Always less than its atomic number
The sum of the number of protons and neutrons present in the nucleus
Always more than the atomic weight
questions.explanation: The mass number (A) of an atom is defined as the total number of nucleons (protons and neutrons) in the nucleus. Mass number = number of protons + number of neutrons. It is always a whole number. The atomic number is only the number of protons, and the atomic weight is an average that may be a decimal due to isotopes.

questions.text: If the volume of a given mass of a gas at 0°C is 29.5cm³. What will be the volume of the gas at 15°C, given that the pressure remains constant?
questions.explanation: Using Charles's Law: V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂ at constant pressure. T₁ = 0°C = 273 K; V₁ = 29.5 cm³; T₂ = 15°C = 288 K. V₂ = 29.5 × 288 ÷ 273 = 31.12 ≈ 31.1 cm³.

questions.text: The sub-atomic particles located in the nucleus of an atom are?
questions.explanation: The nucleus of an atom contains two types of subatomic particles: protons (positively charged) and neutrons (no charge). Electrons are negatively charged particles found outside the nucleus, orbiting in energy shells. Ions are not subatomic particles but atoms that have gained or lost electrons.

questions.text: The mass of silver deposited when a current of 10A is passed through a solution of silver salt for 4830s is    [Ag = 108, F = 96500 Cmol-1]
Which of the following properties is not peculiar to matter?
options: Kinetic energy of particles increases from solid to gas
Random motion of particles increases from gas to solid
Orderliness of particles increases from gas to liquid
Random motion of particles increases from liquid to gas
questions.explanation: Random motion of particles increases from solid to gas, not from gas to solid. Gas particles have the highest kinetic energy and random motion; solid particles have the least. Option B states the opposite of what is true, making it the incorrect (not peculiar to matter) statement.

questions.text: The alkyl group can be represented by the general formula
The weakest attractive force that can be observed between two molecules is
When ammonia and hydrogen ion bond together to form ammonium ion, the bond formed is called
questions.explanation: When NH₃ donates its lone pair of electrons to H⁺ to form NH₄⁺, a dative covalent (coordinate) bond is formed: NH₃ + H⁺ → NH₄⁺. In a dative bond, both electrons in the bond come from one atom (the nitrogen in NH₃). This is a special type of covalent bond — also called a coordinate bond.

questions.text: The reaction between an organic acid and an alcohol in the presence of an acid catalyst is known as
questions.explanation: Esterification is the reaction between a carboxylic acid (organic acid) and an alcohol, catalyzed by a concentrated acid (usually H₂SO₄), to produce an ester and water: RCOOH + R'OH ⇌ RCOOR' + H₂O. Saponification is the reverse (alkaline hydrolysis of esters); dehydration removes water to form alkenes.

questions.text: If a gold bar and a silver bar are tied together firmly and left for years, some of the gold particles will be found in the silver bar due to
questions.explanation: Diffusion is the spontaneous net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to one of lower concentration. Even in solids, atoms can slowly diffuse into adjacent materials over very long periods, explaining why gold atoms migrate into the silver bar.

questions.text: which of the following chlorides would exhibit the least ionic character
Calculate the volume of 0.5 mol dm-3 H2SO4 that is neutralized by 25cm3 of 0.1 mol dm-3 NaOH
Cast iron is used in making
questions.explanation: Cast iron, which contains about 3–4% carbon, is hard but brittle. It is used in making stoves, cookers, manhole covers, engine blocks, and pipes. Wrought iron (low carbon) is used for chains and ornamental work; mild steel is used for nails, rods, and sheets.

questions.text: The shape of ammonia molecules is
questions.explanation: NH₃ has 3 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair of electrons around the nitrogen. The lone pair repels the bonding pairs more strongly, compressing the H-N-H bond angle to ~107°. This gives a trigonal pyramidal shape (not tetrahedral, which is the electron geometry).

questions.text: In which of the following reactions has the oxidation number of nitrogen increased
If one of the following oxides is heated with hydrogen or carbon using a Bunsen burner, it is not reduced to the metal. Which one is it?
questions.explanation: Magnesium is a very reactive metal (high in the electrochemical series) and its oxide (MgO) is very stable. It cannot be reduced by hydrogen or carbon at Bunsen burner temperatures. Lead oxide, copper oxide, and tin oxide are oxides of less reactive metals and can be reduced to their metals by H₂ or C at moderate temperatures.

questions.text: According to the kinetic theory, an absence in temperature causes the kinetic energy of particles to
questions.explanation: According to the kinetic theory, the kinetic energy of particles is directly proportional to absolute temperature. At absolute zero (0 K), temperature is absent and particle motion theoretically ceases completely, so kinetic energy becomes zero.

questions.text: What is the product of the electrolysis of aqueous sodium chloride (NaCl) using inert electrodes?
options: Hydrogen gas at the cathode and chlorine gas at the anode
Hydrogen gas at the cathode and oxygen gas at the anode
Sodium metal at the cathode and chlorine gas at the anode
Sodium metal at the cathode and oxygen gas at the anode
questions.explanation: In the electrolysis of concentrated aqueous NaCl: at the cathode, H⁺ ions from water are preferentially discharged over Na⁺ ions, producing hydrogen gas (2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂). At the anode, Cl⁻ ions are preferentially discharged over OH⁻ ions (in concentrated solution), producing chlorine gas (2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻). The remaining solution becomes sodium hydroxide.

questions.text:
Consider the equation below:
Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 6Fe²⁺ + 14H⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + 6Fe³⁺ + 7H₂O
The oxidation number of chromium changes from
questions.explanation: In Cr₂O₇²⁻: 2x + 7(−2) = −2 → 2x = 12 → x = +6. In the product Cr³⁺, the oxidation number is +3. Chromium is reduced from +6 to +3. Answer: B.

questions.text: In the troposphere, the two types of pollutants are?
questions.explanation: Tropospheric pollutants are classified into two main types: gaseous pollutants (such as CO, SO₂, NO₂, and hydrocarbons) and particulate pollutants (such as dust, smoke, soot, and aerosols). This classification is based on the physical state of the pollutant, which determines how it disperses and causes harm in the atmosphere.

questions.text: To what volume must 300 cm³ of 0.60 M sodium hydroxide solution be diluted to give a 0.40 M solution?
questions.explanation: Using C₁V₁ = C₂V₂. C₁ = 0.60 M, V₁ = 300 cm³, C₂ = 0.40 M. V₂ = (0.60 × 300)/0.40 = 180/0.40 = 450 cm³. The solution must be diluted to a total volume of 450 cm³.

questions.text: Kerosene is commonly used to remove the red colour stain of palm oil from clothes because it
options: Helps to spread the oil over a larger surface area
Makes the oil evaporate easily by dissolving it
Helps to dilute the oil and reduce its colour
Reacts with the oil to form an odourless compound

questions.text: Crude petroleum is converted to useful products by the process of?
questions.explanation: Crude petroleum is a complex mixture of hydrocarbons with different boiling points. Fractional distillation separates these hydrocarbons by heating crude oil and condensing the vapours at different temperatures in a fractionating column, yielding fractions such as petrol, kerosene, diesel, and lubricating oil.

questions.text: Aluminium hydroxide is used in the dyeing industry as a?
questions.explanation: A mordant is a substance used to fix dyes onto fabrics by forming a chemical bridge between the dye and the fibre. Aluminium hydroxide Al(OH)₃ acts as a mordant in the dyeing industry. It precipitates onto the fabric and binds to both the fibre and the dye molecules, producing a more permanent and vibrant colour.

The table shows the compositions of the atmosphere of planet X: CO₂ = 4%, N₂ = 72%, O₂ = 24%. Which of these gases are present in higher percentages on earth?
questions.explanation: On earth: N₂ ≈ 78%, O₂ ≈ 21%, CO₂ ≈ 0.04%. On planet X: CO₂ = 4%, N₂ = 72%, O₂ = 24%. Comparing each gas: CO₂ on planet X (4%) is far higher than on earth (0.04%). O₂ on planet X (24%) is higher than on earth (21%). N₂ on earth (78%) is higher than on planet X (72%). The gases present in higher percentages on planet X compared to earth are CO₂ and O₂.

questions.text: A given volume of methane diffuses in 20s. how long will it take the same volume of sulphur(IV) oxide to diffuse under the same conditions    [C = 12, H = 1, S = 32, O = 16]
An emulsion may be produced by shaking a detergent solution with
In the extraction of iron, the waste gas from the furnace is a mixture of
questions.explanation: In the blast furnace, hot air (containing N₂) is blasted in and coke reacts with oxygen and CO₂ to form CO. The waste gases leaving the furnace are therefore a mixture of N₂ (from the blast of air), CO (reducing agent), and CO₂ (product of reduction reactions).

questions.text: NH3(g)  +  HCI(g)  → NH4CI(s) The entropy change in the system is
The gas which causes global warming is?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is the primary greenhouse gas responsible for global warming. It traps heat from the sun in the earth's atmosphere by absorbing infrared radiation, preventing it from escaping into space. Human activities such as burning fossil fuels and deforestation increase CO₂ levels, intensifying the greenhouse effect.

questions.text: Calculate the amount in moles of silver deposited when 9650 C of electricity is passed through a solution of silver salt [F = 96500 C mol⁻¹]
questions.explanation: Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag (one mole of electrons deposits one mole of Ag). Moles of electrons = charge/F = 9650/96500 = 0.10 mol. Therefore moles of Ag deposited = 0.10 mol.

Which process(es) is/are involved in the turning of starch iodide paper blue-black by chlorine gas?
options: chlorine attacks the starch to give the blue-black colour
chlorine attacks the iodide ion to give the blue-black colour
chlorine oxidizes the iodide ion to produce iodine which attacks the starch to give the blue-black colour
iodine attacks the starch to give the blue-black colour
questions.explanation: The mechanism involves two steps: (1) Chlorine oxidizes iodide ions in the paper to iodine: Cl₂ + 2I⁻ → 2Cl⁻ + I₂. (2) The iodine (I₂) produced forms an intense blue-black complex with the starch. Chlorine itself does not produce the blue-black colour directly — it is the liberated iodine that reacts with starch.

questions.text: What is eutrophication?
options: The release of harmful chemicals into water bodies
The excessive growth of algae due to nutrient enrichment
The presence of heavy metals in water
The formation of oil slicks on water surfaces
questions.explanation: Eutrophication is the process by which a water body becomes enriched with nutrients, particularly nitrates and phosphates from agricultural runoff and sewage. This triggers excessive growth of algae and aquatic plants (algal bloom). When the algae die and decompose, bacteria consume large amounts of oxygen, leading to oxygen depletion and the death of fish and other aquatic organisms.

questions.text: In the industrial production of H₂ from water gas, the CO₂ produced along with the H₂ is removed by
questions.explanation:
Water gas shift reaction:

CO + H₂O → CO₂ + H₂
This produces hydrogen but also carbon dioxide as a byproduct.
CO₂ removal method:

In industrial hydrogen production from water gas, CO₂ is removed by washing under pressure, where the gas mixture is passed through water under high pressure to dissolve and remove the carbon dioxide.

questions.text: In the table above, the two compounds that will combine in the presence of an acid catalyst to form compound V are
questions.explanation: Compound V is an ester (RCOOR'). Esters are formed by acid-catalyzed esterification: RCOOH (carboxylic acid = IV) + ROH (alcohol = I) → RCOOR' + H₂O. Therefore compounds I and IV combine to produce compound V.

questions.text: The refreshing and characteristic taste of soda water and other soft drinks is as a result of the presence of
questions.explanation: The refreshing taste and fizz of soda water and carbonated soft drinks is due to dissolved carbon (IV) oxide (CO₂). CO₂ dissolves under pressure to form carbonic acid (H₂CO₃), giving the drink its characteristic slightly acidic, tangy taste. When the pressure is released, CO₂ escapes as bubbles.

questions.text: Alkanes are used mainly?
questions.explanation: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons that burn readily in oxygen to release large amounts of heat. Their primary use is as fuels, methane (natural gas) for domestic heating and cooking, butane for camping gas, petrol for vehicles, and diesel for industrial engines. Hydrogenation of oils uses hydrogen gas with a nickel catalyst, not alkanes.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs of substances will react further with oxygen to form a higher oxide?
questions.explanation: SO₂ can be further oxidized to SO₃ (a higher oxide): 2SO₂ + O₂ → 2SO₃. NO can be further oxidized to NO₂: 2NO + O₂ → 2NO₂. CO₂ and H₂O are already fully oxidized and cannot react further with oxygen. CO can be oxidized to CO₂, but CO₂ itself cannot go higher.

questions.text: 2H2 + O2  → 2H2O  ΔH = -571Kj  In equation above, how much heat will be liberated if 12.0g of hydrogen is burnt in excess oxygen?
Zinc and carbon rods are used as anode and cathode respectively in a
Which of the following factors does NOT affect the rate of a chemical reaction?
questions.explanation: The rate of a chemical reaction is affected by concentration of reactants, temperature, surface area, presence of a catalyst, and light (for some reactions). The molecular weight of products has no effect on the rate of the reaction, as products are formed after the reaction occurs and do not influence how quickly reactants are converted.

questions.text: In the extraction of Aluminium, the silica impurity is removed by
questions.explanation: In the Bayer process for refining bauxite ore, silica (SiO₂) impurity is removed by dissolving the ore in hot concentrated sodium hydroxide solution. SiO₂ reacts with NaOH: SiO₂ + 2NaOH → Na₂SiO₃ + H₂O. The silicate dissolves and is later precipitated out, while aluminium hydroxide is filtered off. However, among the given options, reaction with H₂SO₄ is closest to an acid-base removal process, though the actual reagent is NaOH.

questions.text: Equal moles of ethyne and hydrogen iodide react to give
The basic particles from which matter could be made up of are as follow, except?
questions.explanation: The basic particles from which matter is made up are atoms, ions, and molecules. Salt is a compound (e.g., NaCl), not a basic particle — it is itself made up of ions. Therefore salt is the odd one out.

questions.text: CH₄(g) + Cl₂(g) → CH₂Cl(s) + HCl(g). The major factor that influences the rate of the reaction above is
questions.explanation: The reaction of methane with chlorine is a free radical substitution reaction initiated by UV light. Light provides the energy to break the Cl-Cl bond homolytically (Cl₂ → 2Cl•), generating chlorine radicals that start the chain reaction. Without light, the reaction does not proceed at room temperature, making light the major rate-determining factor.

questions.text: Trioxonitrate(V) acid is not used for preparing hydrogen gas from metals because it
The heat of formation of ethene, C₂H₄ is 50 kJ mol⁻¹ and that of ethane, C₂H₆ is -82 kJ mol⁻¹. Calculate the heat evolved in the process: C₂H₄ + H₂ → C₂H₆
questions.explanation: Using Hess's Law: ΔH(reaction) = ΔHf(products) - ΔHf(reactants). ΔH = ΔHf(C₂H₆) - ΔHf(C₂H₄) - ΔHf(H₂) = -82 - 50 - 0 = -132 kJ mol⁻¹. The negative sign confirms the hydrogenation of ethene to ethane is exothermic.

questions.text: Iron is often galvanized in order to
questions.explanation: Iron is galvanized to protect it against corrosion. The zinc coating prevents rust formation by acting as both a physical barrier and a sacrificial anode that corrodes preferentially to the iron beneath.

questions.text: Which of the following compounds is used as a gaseous fuel?
questions.explanation: CH₃-CH₂-CH₂-CH₃ is butane, a saturated alkane widely used as a gaseous fuel in LPG (liquefied petroleum gas). Option B is propyne (an alkyne), D is propene (an alkene) — both are flammable but not common domestic gaseous fuels. Option A is not a real stable compound.

questions.text: When water boilers are used for a long period of time, the solid substances left behind as scale are
The most abundant element on the earth’s crust is
What accounts for the low melting and boiling points of covalent molecules?
questions.explanation: Covalent molecules are held together by weak van der Waals (intermolecular) forces between molecules. Little energy is needed to overcome these forces, resulting in low melting and boiling points. The strong covalent bonds within the molecule are not broken during melting or boiling.

questions.text: The only metal that is anti-bacterial is?
questions.explanation: Copper has well-established antibacterial (oligodynamic) properties. Copper ions are toxic to bacteria and disrupt their cell membranes and enzyme systems, killing them on contact. This property is used in copper plumbing, hospital surfaces, and medical devices to reduce bacterial contamination. Iron, sodium, and aluminium do not possess significant antibacterial properties.

questions.text: Liquid black soap is made by boiling palm oil with liquid extract of ash. The function of the ash is to provide the?
questions.explanation: Soap is made by saponification — the reaction of a fat or oil with a strong alkali. Ash extract contains potassium carbonate and potassium hydroxide, which are alkaline. The ash provides the alkali needed to react with palm oil (triglycerides) to form soap (potassium salts of fatty acids) and glycerol.

questions.text: A chemical widely used as a fertilizer is?
questions.explanation: Nitrochalk is a widely used nitrogen fertilizer consisting of a mixture of ammonium nitrate and calcium carbonate (limestone). It supplies nitrogen to plants in the form of ammonium and nitrate ions. Galena is lead sulphide (ore of lead), bauxite is aluminium ore, and emerald is a gemstone — none of these are fertilizers.

questions.text: Aluminium hydroxide is used in the dyeing industry as a
A constituent common to moist air, it gradually rusts. This is due to the formation of
Which of the following is not an alkali?
questions.explanation: An alkali is a soluble base. Al(OH)₃ is amphoteric — it acts as both an acid and a base — and is insoluble in water, so it is not classified as an alkali. Ca(OH)₂ (slightly soluble), NH₃ (forms NH₄OH in water), and NaOH are all alkalis.

questions.text: Calculate the amount in moles of a gas which occupies 10.5 dm³ at 6 atm and 30°C [R = 0.082 atm dm³ K⁻¹ mol⁻¹]
questions.explanation: Using the ideal gas equation PV = nRT. T = 30 + 273 = 303 K. n = PV/RT = (6 × 10.5)/(0.082 × 303) = 63/24.846 = 2.536 mol.

questions.text: Which of the following types of bonding does not involve the formation of new substances?
questions.explanation: Metallic bonding occurs between metal atoms where electrons are delocalised in a "sea" of electrons. This type of bonding holds metal atoms together in a lattice but does not involve the formation of a new chemical substance. Covalent, co-ordinate, and electrovalent (ionic) bonding all involve the combination of different atoms or ions to form new compounds.

questions.text: Using the metal activity series, the metal that can liberate hydrogen gas from steam is?
questions.explanation: Only metals above hydrogen in the reactivity series can displace hydrogen from water or steam. Iron is sufficiently reactive to liberate hydrogen from steam at high temperatures: 3Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂. Copper, tin, and lead are all below or at the level of hydrogen in the reactivity series and cannot liberate hydrogen from steam.

questions.text: The products of the thermal decomposition of ammonium trioxonitrate(v) are?
questions.explanation: Ammonium trioxonitrate(V) is NH₄NO₃. On gentle thermal decomposition: NH₄NO₃ → N₂O + 2H₂O. N₂O is dinitrogen monoxide, also called Nitrogen(I) oxide or laughing gas. At higher temperatures it can decompose further, but the standard products at moderate heating are Nitrogen(I) oxide and water.

questions.text: Elements in the same periodic table have the same
The mass of silver deposited when a current of 10 A is passed through a solution of silver salt for 4830 s is [Ag = 108, F = 96500 C mol⁻¹]
questions.explanation: Charge = I × t = 10 × 4830 = 48300 C. Moles of electrons = 48300/96500 = 0.5 mol. Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag, so moles of Ag = 0.5 mol. Mass of Ag = 0.5 × 108 = 54.0 g.

questions.text: The general formula of alkanones is
questions.explanation: Alkanones (ketones) have the general formula RCOR', where R and R' are alkyl groups flanking the carbonyl (C=O) group. RCHO is an aldehyde; RCOOH is a carboxylic acid; RCOOR is an ester.

questions.text: The principle of column chromatography is based on the ability of the constituents to
options: React with the solvent in the column
React with each other in the solvent in the column
Dissolve in each other in the column
Move at different speeds in the column
questions.explanation: Column chromatography separates mixtures based on the ability of components to move at different speeds through the stationary phase. Components with greater affinity for the stationary phase move more slowly, while those preferring the mobile phase move faster, achieving separation.

questions.text: How much of 5g of a radioactive element whose half life is 50 days remains after 200 days?
questions.explanation: Number of half-lives = 200 ÷ 50 = 4. Remaining mass = 5 × (½)⁴ = 5 × 1/16 = 5 ÷ 16 = 0.3125 g ≈ 0.31 g.

questions.text: Identify the reducing agent in the following reaction: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu
questions.explanation: A reducing agent is the substance that loses electrons (is oxidised) in a redox reaction. In this reaction, Zn goes from oxidation state 0 to +2 in ZnSO₄ — it loses electrons and is oxidised. Zn is therefore the reducing agent. Cu²⁺ gains electrons and is reduced from +2 to 0, making CuSO₄ the oxidising agent.

questions.text: The ions responsible for permanent hardness in water are sulphates of
questions.explanation: Permanent hardness in water is caused by dissolved calcium sulphate (CaSO₄) and magnesium sulphate (MgSO₄) — the sulphate salts of Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺. Unlike temporary hardness caused by bicarbonates, permanent hardness cannot be removed by boiling. It requires treatment with washing soda (Na₂CO₃) or ion exchange to remove the Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions.

questions.text: What type of reaction is involved in the formation of alkanols from alkenes?
questions.explanation: Alkanols (alcohols) are formed from alkenes by the addition of water across the C=C double bond in a reaction called hydration. For example: CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O → CH₃CH₂OH. This is an addition reaction because atoms are added across the double bond without any atoms being removed. The reaction requires a catalyst (concentrated H₂SO₄ or H₃PO₄) and heat.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of an endothermic reaction?
options: Combustion of propane (C₃H₈) to produce carbon dioxide (CO₂) and water (H₂O).
Burning of methane (CH₄) in the presence of oxygen
Formation of table salt (NaCl) from sodium (Na) and chlorine (Cl₂).
Decomposition of hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) into water (H₂O) and oxygen (O₂).
questions.explanation: An endothermic reaction absorbs heat energy from the surroundings (ΔH is positive). The decomposition of hydrogen peroxide (2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂) is endothermic — energy must be supplied to break the O-O bonds in H₂O₂. Combustion of propane, burning of methane, and formation of sodium chloride are all exothermic reactions that release heat energy.

questions.text: 32g of anhydrous copper(ii)tetraoxosulphate(vi) dissolved in 1dm³ of water generated 13.0kJ of heat. The heat of solution is?
questions.explanation: Molar mass of anhydrous CuSO₄ = 64 + 32 + 64 = 160 g/mol. Moles dissolved = 32 ÷ 160 = 0.2 mol. Heat generated = 13.0 kJ for 0.2 mol. Heat of solution per mole = 13.0 ÷ 0.2 = 65.0 kJ/mol.

questions.text: A gas exerts pressure on its container because
options: Some of its molecules are moving faster than others
Of the collision of the molecules with each other
Of the mass of the molecules of gas
The molecules of a gas collide with the walls of the container

questions.text: The carbon atoms in ethane are
questions.explanation: Ethane (CH₃-CH₃) contains only C-C and C-H single bonds. Each carbon forms 4 single bonds using sp³ hybridization (one s orbital + three p orbitals combine to form 4 equivalent sp³ hybrid orbitals arranged tetrahedrally). sp² is for alkenes; sp is for alkynes; sp⁴ does not exist.

questions.text: Which of the following describes the chemical property of acids?
questions.explanation: A standard chemical property of acids is their reaction with carbonates. Acid + metal carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide. Example: 2HCl + Na₂CO₃ → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂. Option B wrongly gives NH₃ as a product; Option C wrongly gives CO₂ from acid + NaOH. Answer: D.

questions.text: The table shows formulae of some ions (Cations: Al³⁺, Ca²⁺, Cu²⁺, Fe³⁺, K⁺; Anions: Br⁻, CO₃²⁻, NO₃⁻, S²⁻, SO₄²⁻). In which of these compounds is the formula not correct?
questions.explanation: Iron(III) has a charge of 3+ and bromide has a charge of 1−. To balance: 1 Fe³⁺ needs 3 Br⁻, giving FeBr₃ as the correct formula. Fe₃Br shown in option C is incorrect. Al₂(SO₄)₃ is correct (2×3+ = 3×2−). Ca(NO₃)₂ is correct (1×2+ = 2×1−). K₂S is correct (2×1+ = 1×2−).

Which of the following statements is true about 2-methylpropane and butane?
options: They have different number of carbon atoms
They are members of same homologous series
They have the same boiling points
questions.explanation: 2-methylpropane and butane are structural isomers — both have the molecular formula C₄H₁₀ and belong to the alkane homologous series. They have the same number of carbon atoms and similar chemical properties, but different boiling points due to different branching.

A gaseous metallic chloride MCl consists of 20.22% of M by mass. The formula of the chloride is? [M = 27, Cl = 35.5]
questions.explanation: Let the formula be MClₙ. % of M = 27 ÷ (27 + 35.5n) × 100 = 20.22. Solving: 27 = 0.2022 × (27 + 35.5n) → 27 = 5.459 + 7.178n → 21.541 = 7.178n → n = 3. The formula is MCl₃. (M = 27 is aluminium, Al, so the compound is AlCl₃.)

questions.text: Acid radicals are present in
questions.explanation: Acid radicals are negatively charged ions (anions) derived from acids. CO₃²⁻ (from H₂CO₃), SO₄²⁻ (from H₂SO₄), and NO₃⁻ (from HNO₃) are all acid radicals. Options A, B, and D each contain a cation (Mg²⁺, Na⁺, K⁺) which are basic radicals, not acid radicals.

questions.text: In the laboratory preparation of oxygen using potassium trioxochlorate(V), tetraoxomanganate(VII) is usually not recommended in modern laboratory because
options: it forms explosive mixture with carbonaceous materials
questions.explanation: Potassium trioxochlorate(V) (KClO₃) is a strong oxidizing agent. When mixed with carbonaceous or organic materials (such as rubber, grease, or carbon), it can form highly explosive mixtures. This safety hazard is the specific reason it is no longer recommended for routine laboratory use.

questions.text: Which of the following typically represents a photochemical reaction
options: Conversion of dinitrogen (IV) oxide to nitrogen(IV) oxide
Conversion of silver halides to grey metallic silver
Decomposition of calcium hydroxide to its oxide
Formation of water from hydrogen and oxygen molecules

options: It forms Tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid with water
