questions.explanation: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu. Moles of Cu = 4.5/64 = 0.0703 mol. Moles of electrons = 2 × 0.0703 = 0.1406 mol. Charge Q = 0.1406 × 96500 = 13570 C. Time t = Q/I = 13570/2.5 = 5428 sec.

questions.text: Environmental pollution is worsened by the release from automobile exhausts of
In the reaction: M + N → P, ΔH = +Q kJ. Which of the following would increase the concentration of the product?
questions.explanation: ΔH = +Q kJ means the forward reaction is endothermic. By Le Chatelier's principle, increasing temperature favours the endothermic (forward) reaction, shifting equilibrium to the right and increasing the concentration of product P. A catalyst increases the rate but does not shift equilibrium. Increasing concentration of P shifts equilibrium backward.

questions.text: The arrangement of particles in crystal lattices can be studied using
questions.explanation: X-ray crystallography is the technique used to study the arrangement of particles in crystal lattices. X-rays have wavelengths comparable to the spacing between atoms in crystals, causing diffraction patterns that reveal the three-dimensional structure of the crystal.

questions.text: If the quantity of oxygen occupying 2.76L container at a pressure of 0.825 atm and 300K is reduced by one-half, what is the pressure exerted by the remaining gas?
questions.explanation: The amount of gas is reduced by half at constant volume and temperature. By the ideal gas law (PV = nRT), pressure is directly proportional to the number of moles at constant V and T. Halving the moles halves the pressure. New pressure = 0.825 ÷ 2 = 0.4125 atm ≈ 0.413 atm.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs cannot be represented with a chemical formula?
questions.explanation: Air is a mixture of gases (N₂, O₂, Ar, CO₂) with variable composition — no fixed formula. Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin with variable composition — no fixed formula. Mixtures and alloys of variable composition cannot be represented by a single chemical formula. Answer: A.

questions.text: An example of an acidic oxide is
questions.explanation: SO₂ is an acidic oxide — it dissolves in water to form sulphurous acid (H₂SO₃) and reacts with bases to form salts. NO and CO are neutral oxides (they do not react with acids or bases to form salts). CuO is a basic oxide (reacts with acids, not with bases).

questions.text: The diagram above. Y is
questions.explanation: In the diagram, Y is the conical flask containing the drying agent through which the gas passes before collection. Concentrated H₂SO₄ is the standard drying agent used to dry acidic or neutral gases in laboratory gas preparation. Z is the thistle funnel for adding acid, and X is the water trough for collection by downward displacement of water.

questions.text: The IUPAC name of the compound CF₃CHBrCl is
questions.explanation: In CF₃CHBrCl: C1 carries the three F atoms, C2 carries Br, Cl, and H. Numbering to give lowest locants: C1 = CF₃ (F gets positions 1,1,1), C2 = CHBrCl (Br and Cl at position 2). Substituents listed alphabetically: bromo before chloro before fluoro. IUPAC name: 1-bromo-1-chloro-2,2,2-trifluoroethane.

questions.text: Iron can be protected from corrosion by coating the surface with
A chemical process in which there is a gain of electrons is known as?
questions.explanation: Reduction is the chemical process in which an atom, ion, or molecule gains electrons. This results in a decrease in oxidation number. The mnemonic OIL RIG (Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain) summarises this: oxidation involves loss of electrons while reduction involves gain of electrons.

questions.text: When an acidic solution is diluted, what happens to its pH?
options: It depends on the specific acid
questions.explanation: Diluting an acidic solution adds more water, which decreases the concentration of H⁺ ions. Since pH = −log[H⁺], a decrease in H⁺ concentration causes the pH to increase (move closer to 7). The solution becomes less acidic but remains acidic — the pH rises toward 7 but does not exceed it on dilution alone.

questions.text: NH₃(g) + HCl(g) → NH₄Cl(g). In the reaction above, increase in pressure will
questions.explanation: By Le Chatelier's principle, increased pressure favours the side with fewer moles of gas. Reactants have 2 moles of gas (NH₃ + HCl) while the product has 1 mole (NH₄Cl). Increased pressure therefore shifts equilibrium to the right, favouring the product. The equilibrium constant is unaffected by pressure.

questions.text: Which of the following is a common property of non-metals?
options: Exist as solids at room temperature
Tend to gain electrons in chemical reactions
Readily form cations in chemical reactions
questions.explanation: Non-metals tend to gain electrons in chemical reactions, forming negatively charged anions. This is because non-metals have high electronegativities and need relatively few electrons to complete their outer shells. High thermal and electrical conductivity are properties of metals. Most non-metals are gases or have low melting points at room temperature, though some like carbon (graphite) are solid. Forming cations is a property of metals.

questions.text: A gas occupies a volume of 1.5 liters at a pressure of 2 atmospheres. If the pressure is increased to 4 atmospheres while the temperature remains constant, what will be the new volume of the gas?
questions.explanation: Using Boyle's Law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂ at constant temperature. P₁ = 2 atm; V₁ = 1.5 L; P₂ = 4 atm. V₂ = P₁V₁ ÷ P₂ = (2 × 1.5) ÷ 4 = 3.0 ÷ 4 = 0.75 litres.

questions.text: The commonest feature of the reactions at the anode is that
What current in amperes will deposit 2.7g of aluminium in 2 hours [Al = 27, f = 96500 C mol-1]
The volume of 2.5 moles of oxygen at s.t.p is
Which of the following alkaline earth metals react more spontaneously with water?
questions.explanation: Reactivity of alkaline earth metals with water increases down Group II: Be < Mg < Ca < Sr < Ba. Strontium (Sr) is the most reactive among the options given, reacting vigorously and spontaneously with cold water to give Sr(OH)₂ and H₂. Be barely reacts with water; Mg reacts only with steam; Ca reacts with cold water but less vigorously than Sr.

questions.text: A chemical reaction is always associated with
options: An increase in the composition of one of the substances
A change in the volume of the reactants
A change in the nature of the reactants

questions.text: Which of the following results in the fall of acid rain?
questions.explanation: Oxides of sulphur (SO₂ and SO₃), released mainly from burning fossil fuels, react with water vapour in the atmosphere to form sulphurous and sulphuric acids, which fall as acid rain. Oxides of nitrogen also contribute, but among the options given, oxides of sulphur is correct.

questions.text: The energy value of petrol can be determined by
questions.explanation: A bomb calorimeter is used to measure the calorific (energy) value of fuels like petrol. The fuel is burned in a sealed oxygen-filled vessel surrounded by water, and the temperature rise is used to calculate the heat released.

questions.text: The raw material used for the smelting of iron ore in a furnace is
25cm3 of a gas X contains Zmolecules at 150C and 75mmHg. How many molecules will 25cmm3 of another gas Y contain at the same temperature and pressure
When 10g of sodium hydroxide is dissolved in 1000cm3 of water, the solution formed is approximately   [Na = 23, H = 1, O = 16]
The gas that can be dried using concentrated Tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid is
A liquid hydrocarbon obtained from fractional distillation of coal tar that is used in the pharmaceutical industry is
questions.explanation: Benzene is obtained from the fractional distillation of coal tar and is an important raw material in the pharmaceutical industry. It is used in the synthesis of drugs, dyes, and plastics. Although xylene and toluene are also obtained from coal tar, benzene is the most fundamental and widely used aromatic compound in pharmaceutical manufacturing.

questions.text: The number of isomers formed by C₆H₁₄ is
questions.explanation:
Alkanes exhibit structural isomerism due to different arrangements of carbon atoms. For hexane (C₆H₁₄), the isomers are:

n-hexane (straight chain)

2-methylpentane (one methyl group on carbon 2)

3-methylpentane (one methyl group on carbon 3)

2,2-dimethylbutane (two methyl groups on carbon 2)

2,3-dimethylbutane (two methyl groups on carbons 2 and 3)


There are 5 structural isomers of hexane.

The number of isomers formed by C₆H₁₄ is 5.

questions.text: To a solution of an unknown compound, a little dilute Tetraoxosulphate (IV) acid was added with some freshly prepared (II) Tetraoxosulphate (VI) Solution. The brown ring observed after the addition of a stream of concentrated  Tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid confirmed the presence of
Ammonium chloride can be separated from its mixture with common salt by
questions.explanation: NH₄Cl sublimes — it converts directly from solid to vapour on heating without melting. NaCl (common salt) does not sublime. Heating the mixture causes NH₄Cl vapour to rise and re-solidify on a cooler surface, separating it cleanly from NaCl.

questions.text: In the laboratory preparation of oxygen, the gas cannot be collected by downward displacement of air because
options: the density of oxygen is greater than that of air
the density of air is nearly the same as that of oxygen
oxygen is a component of air
questions.explanation: Oxygen cannot be collected by downward displacement of air because oxygen is itself a major component of air (~21%). Introducing O₂ into air simply mixes with the air already present, making it impossible to collect a pure sample. O₂ is collected over water (upward displacement of water) or by upward displacement of air instead.

questions.text: The pressure of 100cm3 of oxygen at 350C is 750mmHg. What will be the volume of the gas if the pressure is reduced to 100mmHg  without changing the temperature
What mass of water is produced when 8.0g of hydriogen reacts with excess oxygen [H = 1, O = 16]
An oxide X02 has a vapour density of 32. What is the atomic mass of X [O = 16]
Which of the following is an example of a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Rusting of iron is a chemical change because a new substance (iron III oxide, Fe₂O₃·XH₂O) with different properties is formed and the process is irreversible. Dissolution of salt, melting of ice, and distillation are all physical changes — no new substances are formed and the changes are reversible.

questions.text: A small quantity of solid ammonium chloride (NH₄Cl) is heated gently in a test tube. The solid gradually disappears producing two gases. Later, a white cloudy deposit was observed on the cooler part of the test tube. The ammonium chloride is said to have undergone
questions.explanation: Ammonium chloride undergoes sublimation when heated - it changes directly from solid to gas (decomposing into NH₃ and HCl), then reforms as a white solid deposit on the cooler parts of the tube when the gases recombine and cool.

questions.text: CH₃C≡CCH(CH₃)₂. The IUPAC nomenclature of the compound above is
questions.explanation: The structure is CH₃-C≡C-CH(CH₃)-CH₃. The longest chain containing the triple bond has 5 carbons (pentyne). Numbering from the end nearer the triple bond: C1=CH₃, C2≡C3, C4=CH with a CH₃ branch, C5=CH₃. The triple bond is at C2 and the methyl branch is at C4. IUPAC name: 4-methylpent-2-yne.

questions.text: Chlorine consisting of two isotopes of mass numbers 35 and 37 in the ratio 3:1 has an atomic mass of 35.5. Calculate the relative abundance of the isotope of mass number 37.
Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂. What happens to zinc in the above reaction?
questions.explanation: In this reaction, zinc (Zn) goes from an oxidation state of 0 in the element to +2 in ZnCl₂. A loss of electrons and an increase in oxidation number constitutes oxidation. Zinc is therefore oxidised. Hydrogen simultaneously goes from +1 in HCl to 0 in H₂ gas, meaning hydrogen is reduced. Zinc is the reducing agent.

questions.text: The structural component that makes detergent dissolve more quickly in water than soap is
An element having the atomic number 17 will resemble which of the following elements having atomic number as given below?
questions.explanation: Atomic number 17 is chlorine, in Group VIIA (halogens) with 7 valence electrons and configuration ending in 3p⁵. Elements in the same group have the same number of valence electrons and similar chemical properties. Atomic number 35 is bromine, also a halogen with 7 valence electrons (configuration ending in 4p⁵). Bromine therefore resembles chlorine most closely.

questions.text: What volume of 0.5 M H₂SO₄ will exactly neutralize 20 cm³ of 0.1 M NaOH solution?
questions.explanation: Reaction: H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. Moles of NaOH = 0.1 × 20/1000 = 0.002 mol. Moles of H₂SO₄ required = 0.002/2 = 0.001 mol. Volume of H₂SO₄ = 0.001/0.5 = 0.002 dm³ = 2.0 cm³.

questions.text: In a flame test for calcium, the flame appears
options: Blue when viewed through a blue glass
Green when viewed through a blue glass
Orange-red when viewed through a blue glass
Brick-red when viewed through a blue glass

questions.text: The pollution from petroleum spillage in rivers and lakes can best be dispersed by
options: Passing of ships through the area

questions.text: 2-methylprop-1-ene is an isomer of?
questions.explanation: 2-methylprop-1-ene has the formula CH₂=C(CH₃)₂ with molecular formula C₄H₈. Structural isomers must have the same molecular formula. But-2-ene (CH₃CH=CHCH₃) also has the formula C₄H₈. Options A, B, and D are C₅ compounds (C₅H₁₀), so only but-2-ene is a correct isomer.

questions.text: Which of the following gases can be collected by the method of downward delivery
What is the principal ore of iron, from which iron is extracted?
questions.explanation: The principal ore of iron used for large-scale extraction is hematite (Fe₂O₃), also spelled haematite. It contains a high percentage of iron and is widely available. Iron is extracted from hematite in a blast furnace using coke and limestone. Bauxite is the ore of aluminium, calcite is a form of calcium carbonate, and magnetite (Fe₃O₄) is another iron ore but less commonly used as the principal source.

questions.text: An example of aliphatic unsaturated hydrocarbon is
Which of the following mixtures of gases is likely to burn in flame
Hydrogen is readily released when dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with
An organic compound which decolourises bromine water is likely to be?
questions.explanation: Bromine water is decolourised by compounds containing a C=C double bond (alkenes) or C≡C triple bond (alkynes) through addition reactions. C₂H₄ is ethene, an alkene with a double bond: C₂H₄ + Br₂ → C₂H₄Br₂ (colourless). C₃H₈, C₂H₆, and C₄H₁₀ are all alkanes, which do not react with bromine water under normal conditions.

questions.text: Detergents are manufactured with straight hydrocarbon chains, is to make them
questions.explanation: Detergents with straight (unbranched) hydrocarbon chains are biodegradable because soil bacteria can break down straight chains enzymatically. Branched-chain detergents resist bacterial degradation and cause persistent foam pollution in water bodies.

questions.text: Which of the following is used as a rocket fuel
According to the kinetic theory of gases, the pressure exerted by a gas is due to?
options: The weight of the gas particles
The attractive forces between gas particles
The collisions of gas particles with the container walls
questions.explanation: According to the kinetic molecular theory, gas particles are in constant random motion and collide elastically with each other and with the walls of their container. The pressure exerted by a gas is the result of these continuous collisions of gas molecules with the container walls. Each collision exerts a small force, and the cumulative effect of billions of collisions per second creates the measurable gas pressure.

questions.text: 8g of CH₄ occupies 11.2 dm³ at S.T.P. What volume would 22g of CH₃CH₂CH₃ occupy under the same condition?
questions.explanation: Molar mass of CH₄ = 16 g/mol. 8g of CH₄ = 8/16 = 0.5 mol, occupying 11.2 dm³ → 1 mol occupies 22.4 dm³ at STP. Molar mass of CH₃CH₂CH₃ (propane) = 44 g/mol. Moles of propane = 22/44 = 0.5 mol. Volume = 0.5 × 22.4 = 11.2 dm³.

questions.text: The nitrogenous compound in dead materials in the soil is converted to
questions.explanation: During ammonification, decomposer bacteria break down nitrogenous compounds in dead organic matter (proteins, nucleic acids) and release ammonia (NH₃). This is the first step in the recycling of nitrogen from dead materials back into the nitrogen cycle.

questions.text: The constituents of Alnico are Aluminium, Nickel and
questions.explanation: Alnico is a magnetic alloy whose name is derived from its constituent elements: Aluminium (Al), Nickel (Ni), and Cobalt (Co). It also contains iron as the base metal. Alnico alloys are used in making permanent magnets for electric motors, microphones, and loudspeakers due to their strong magnetic properties.

questions.text: Pollution of underground water by metal ions is very likely in a soil that has high
The boiling of fat and aqueous caustic soda is referred as
When iron is exposed to moist air, it gradually rusts. This is due to the formation of
The group VIII elements are the inert gases because they
options: have lone pair of electrons on their valence shells
all have completely filled valence shells
questions.explanation: Noble gases (Group VIII/Group 18) are chemically inert because their outermost electron shells are completely filled. Helium has 2 electrons (full 1s²), and the rest have 8 electrons in their outermost shell (ns²np⁶), achieving stable octet configurations. This complete filling leaves no tendency to gain, lose, or share electrons, making them unreactive. They are not solids at room temperature and exist as monoatomic gases.

questions.text: Which of the following types of alkanols undergo oxidation to produce alkanoic acids?
questions.explanation: Only primary alkanols (I) are oxidized to produce alkanoic acids. Primary alkanols oxidize first to aldehydes, then to carboxylic (alkanoic) acids. Secondary alkanols oxidize to ketones (not acids), and tertiary alkanols resist oxidation.

questions.text: Alkanols have the general molecular formula
questions.explanation: Alkanols (alcohols derived from alkanes) have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH, where the CₙH₂ₙ₊₁ part is the alkyl group attached to the hydroxyl (-OH) functional group. For example, methanol is CH₃OH (n=1) and ethanol is C₂H₅OH (n=2).

questions.text: The enzyme used in the hydrolysis of starch to dextrin and maltose is
questions.explanation: Amylase is the enzyme responsible for the hydrolysis of starch, breaking it down first into dextrin and then into maltose. Zymase converts sugars to ethanol; sucrase hydrolyses sucrose; lactase hydrolyses lactose.

questions.text: In the industrial production of H2 from natural gas, the CO2 produced along with the H2 is removed by
options: Passing the mixture into lime water

questions.text: The acid anhydride that will produce weak acid in water is
questions.explanation: CO₂ dissolves in water to form carbonic acid (H₂CO₃), which is a weak acid: CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃. SO₃ forms strong H₂SO₄; NO₂ forms strong HNO₃ (and weak HNO₂ in equal measure); SO₂ forms weak H₂SO₃ — but CO₂ producing carbonic acid is the clearest example of a weak acid from an acid anhydride.

questions.text:
Which of the following are mixtures?
I. Petroleum
II. Rubber latex
III. Vulcanizer's solution
IV. Carbon sulphide
questions.explanation: Petroleum is a mixture of hydrocarbons; rubber latex is a colloidal mixture of rubber particles in water; vulcanizer's solution is a mixture of rubber dissolved in a solvent. Carbon disulphide (CS₂) is a pure chemical compound, not a mixture. Therefore I, II and III are mixtures.

questions.text: The most important use of hydrogen is in the
The periodic classification is an arrangement of the elements in order of their
questions.explanation: The modern periodic table (based on Moseley's work) arranges elements in order of increasing atomic number (number of protons). Earlier versions (Mendeleev's) used atomic mass, but the modern classification is based strictly on atomic number, which determines the chemical properties of elements.

questions.text: In which of the following reactuions does reduction take place
Sugar is separated from its impurities by
Metalloids are also referred to as
The formula for ethyl butanoate is
Neutrons were discovered by?
questions.explanation: James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932 by bombarding beryllium with alpha particles and detecting the uncharged particle emitted. Rutherford discovered the proton and the nucleus, J.J. Thomson discovered the electron, and Dalton proposed the atomic theory but discovered no subatomic particles.

questions.text: A trihydric alkanol is
Which of the following statements does NOT show Rutherford's account of Nuclear Theory? An atom contains a region
options: which is massive and can cause deflection of a few projectiles
which is very large and in which close to 98% of projectiles pass undeflected
questions.explanation: Rutherford's nuclear model described the nucleus as a tiny, dense, positively charged centre (options B and C). Most alpha particles passed straight through (option D — though the nucleus is tiny, not large). However, Rutherford did NOT identify neutrons — that was Chadwick in 1932. Rutherford's model only described protons in the nucleus, not neutrons. Option A is not part of Rutherford's original nuclear theory.

questions.text: Which separation technique is used to separate different pigments in a mixture based on their affinity for a stationary phase and a mobile phase?
questions.explanation: Chromatography separates components of a mixture based on their different affinities for a stationary phase and a mobile phase. Components that interact more strongly with the stationary phase move more slowly, while those that interact more with the mobile phase move faster. This differential migration separates pigments and other mixture components. It is widely used in paper chromatography, thin-layer chromatography, and column chromatography.

questions.text: The reddish-brown rust on iron roofing sheets consists of
questions.explanation: Rust is hydrated iron (III) oxide, represented as Fe₂O₃·XH₂O (where X is variable). It is formed by the oxidation of iron in the presence of water and oxygen. The reddish-brown colour is characteristic of Fe₂O₃ (iron III oxide) in its hydrated form.

questions.text: Which of the following solutions containing only hydroxyl ions will liberate hydrogen gas when reacted with magnesium metal
Which group does calcium belong to in the periodic table?
questions.explanation: Calcium (Ca) has atomic number 20 and electron configuration [Ar] 4s². It is in Group IIA (Group 2) of the periodic table, known as the alkaline earth metals. This group includes beryllium, magnesium, calcium, strontium, barium, and radium. Alkali metals are Group IA, halogens are Group VIIA, and noble gases are Group VIII/0.

questions.text: The correct order of increasing boiling points of the following  compounds C3H7OH, C7H16 and C4H10 is
Tartaric acid is used industrially to
questions.explanation: Tartaric acid is used industrially to make baking powder. It acts as the acid component in baking powder, reacting with sodium bicarbonate to release CO₂ gas, which causes dough to rise.

questions.text: The chlorinated alkane often used industrially to remove grease is?
questions.explanation: Tetrachloromethane (CCl₄) is a non-polar solvent widely used industrially as a degreasing agent because it dissolves grease and oils effectively without itself being flammable. Its non-polarity allows it to interact with and dissolve the non-polar grease molecules through dispersion forces.

questions.text: The sulphide which is insoluble in dilute hydrochloric acid is
Which trace gas in the atmosphere plays a significant role in the greenhouse effect?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is a trace gas (about 0.04% of the atmosphere) that plays a major role in the greenhouse effect. It absorbs infrared radiation emitted from the earth's surface and re-radiates it, trapping heat in the atmosphere. Nitrogen and oxygen make up most of the atmosphere but do not absorb infrared radiation significantly. Argon is chemically inert and does not contribute to the greenhouse effect.

questions.text: In the laboratory preparation of ethyl ethanoate, the water present in the mixture is removed using
questions.explanation: In the preparation of ethyl ethanoate (ester), concentrated H₂SO₄ serves a dual role: it acts as both the catalyst for the esterification reaction and as a dehydrating agent to remove water produced, driving the equilibrium toward ester formation. Anhydrous CaCl₂ is not used as it can complex with the ester.

questions.text: In the laboratory preparation of trioxonitrate (V) acid, the nitrogen (IV) oxide formed as a by-product is removed by
options: cooling the acid solution with cold water
bubbling air through the acid solution
questions.explanation: In the preparation of HNO₃, NO₂ (nitrogen IV oxide) dissolves in the acid giving it a brown colour. To remove it, air is bubbled through the acid solution: 4NO₂ + O₂ + 2H₂O → 4HNO₃. The oxygen in the air oxidises the dissolved NO₂, converting it to more HNO₃ and producing a colourless acid.

questions.text: Which of the following is a physical change?
questions.explanation: A physical change alters the form or appearance of a substance without changing its chemical composition. Freezing ice cream involves a change of state (liquid to solid) — no new substance is formed. Exposing white phosphorus to air, burning kerosene, and dissolving calcium in water all involve chemical reactions that produce new substances.

questions.text: The stability of the noble gases is due to the fact that they
options: Have duplet or octet electron configurations
Belong to group zero of the periodic table
Have no electron in their outermost shells

questions.text: In countries where the temperature fall below 273 K, salt is always spilled on the road in order to
options: increase the density of the ice
reduce the freezing point of ice
questions.explanation: Salt (NaCl) is spread on icy roads to reduce the freezing point of water (freezing point depression). Dissolving salt in water lowers its freezing point below 0°C (273 K), causing ice to melt even at sub-zero temperatures and preventing refreezing.

questions.text: Diamond is a bad conductor of electricity because its bonding electrons are used in
questions.explanation: In diamond, each carbon atom forms four strong covalent bonds with four neighbouring carbon atoms in a giant tetrahedral lattice. All four valence electrons of each carbon are used in covalent bond formation, leaving no free (delocalized) electrons available to carry electric current. This is why diamond is a non-conductor of electricity.

questions.text: The radioisotope used in industrial radiography for the rapid checking of faults in welds and casting is
questions.explanation: Cobalt-60 is used in industrial radiography because it emits high-energy gamma rays that can penetrate metal welds and castings. The gamma rays expose photographic film on the other side, revealing any internal flaws or defects. Carbon-14 is used in radiocarbon dating; iodine-131 is used in thyroid diagnosis/treatment; phosphorus-32 is used in biological research.

questions.text: The furring of kettles is caused by the presence in water of
the principal constituent of natural gas is methane
Cathode rays cause an object placed behind a perforated anode to cast a shadow on the screen. This observation shows that the rays
questions.explanation: For a shadow to be cast, the rays must travel in straight lines from the source. If they were scattered or bent around the object, a sharp shadow would not be formed.

questions.text: A given amount of gas occupies 10.0 dm³ at 4 atm and 273°C. The number of moles of the gas present is? [Molar volume of gas at s.t.p = 22.4 dm³]
questions.explanation: First convert to STP using combined gas law: V(STP) = P₁V₁T₂/(T₁P₂) = (4 × 10 × 273)/(546 × 1) = 20.0 dm³. Note: T₁ = 273°C + 273 = 546 K, T₂ = 273 K (STP). Moles = 20.0/22.4 = 0.89 mol.

questions.text: 6AgNO3(aq)  +  PH3(g) +    3H2O(l)      →    6Ag(s)+   H3PO3(aq)   +    6HNO3(aq)  In the reaction above, the reducing agent is
When at equilibrium, which of the reactions below will shift to the right if the pressure is increased and the temperature is kept constant
Which of the gas laws does this graph illustrate?
questions.explanation: The graph shows volume on the y-axis and temperature in Kelvin on the x-axis, producing a straight line through the origin. This represents a direct proportionality (V ∝ T at constant pressure), which illustrates Charles's Law: the volume of a fixed mass of gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature at constant pressure.

questions.text: In the diagram above, X is the
questions.explanation: In the energy profile diagram, X is the arrow showing the difference in energy level between the reactants and the products. This energy difference is the enthalpy change (ΔH) of the reaction. Since products are lower in energy than reactants, ΔH is negative (exothermic). The activation energy would be measured from reactants to the peak, not between reactants and products.

questions.text: What is the main source of carbon monoxide (CO) in urban areas?
questions.explanation: In urban areas, the primary source of carbon monoxide (CO) is vehicle emissions. CO is produced by the incomplete combustion of petrol and diesel in internal combustion engines when there is insufficient oxygen. High concentrations of CO in cities are directly linked to traffic density. Volcanic eruptions and forest fires contribute CO but are not the main urban sources.

questions.text: Which of the following is an electrolyte
Strong acids can be distinguished from weak acids by any of the following methods, EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Litmus paper only indicates whether a solution is acidic or basic — it turns red for any acid regardless of strength. It cannot distinguish between a strong acid and a weak acid. Conductivity measurement distinguishes them because strong acids fully ionise and conduct electricity much better. pH measurement distinguishes them since strong acids have lower pH at the same concentration. Heat of neutralisation also differs between strong and weak acids.

questions.text: It is difficult to achieve an orderly arrangement of the molecules of a gas because they
options: Have little force attraction between them
Can collide with one another in the container

questions.text: The colour of litmus in an alkaline medium is
questions.explanation: Litmus is a pH indicator that turns blue in alkaline (basic) solutions and red in acidic solutions. In a neutral solution, it remains purple. Therefore, in an alkaline medium, litmus turns blue.

questions.text: An isotope has an atomic number of 15 and a mass number of 31. The number of protons it contains is
questions.explanation: The atomic number of an element equals the number of protons in its nucleus. Since the atomic number is 15, the atom contains 15 protons. The number of neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 31 − 15 = 16.

questions.text: Which of these require crystallization most?
questions.explanation: Drug making requires crystallization most because pharmaceuticals must be highly purified, and crystallization is the primary method to achieve the purity levels required for safe and effective medications.

questions.text: What is the concentration of a solution containing 2 g of NaOH in 100 cm³ of solution? [Na = 23, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.explanation: Molar mass of NaOH = 23 + 16 + 1 = 40 g mol⁻¹. Moles of NaOH = 2/40 = 0.05 mol. Volume = 100 cm³ = 0.1 dm³. Concentration = 0.05/0.1 = 0.50 mol dm⁻³.

questions.text: A particle that contains 9 protons, 10 neutrons and 10 electrons is
questions.explanation: The particle has 9 protons (atomic number = 9, so it is fluorine) but 10 electrons. Since electrons (10) > protons (9), the particle carries a net negative charge of -1. It is therefore a negative ion (anion) — specifically the fluoride ion, F⁻.

questions.text: The property of metal that makes it suitable as a catalyst is
questions.explanation: Transition metals act as catalysts because they have partially filled d-orbitals that allow them to form temporary bonds with reactants, adopt variable oxidation states, and adsorb reactant molecules — all of which lower the activation energy.

questions.text: According to Charles' law, the volume of a gas becomes zero at
questions.explanation: Charles' Law states V ∝ T (in Kelvin). Extrapolating the V-T graph to V = 0 gives T = 0 K, which corresponds to -273°C (absolute zero). At this theoretical temperature, an ideal gas would have zero volume.

questions.text: During the fractional distillation of crude oil, the fraction that distils at 200–250°C is
questions.explanation: During fractional distillation of crude oil, different fractions condense at different temperature ranges. Kerosene (paraffin) distils between approximately 150–250°C. Petrol distils below 150°C, diesel distils between 250–350°C, and bitumen remains as a residue above 350°C. The fraction that distils at 200–250°C is kerosene.

questions.text: In the electrolysis of CuSO4(aq) using platinum electrodes, the reaction at the anode is
The principle which states that no two electrons in the same orbital of an atom have the same value for all four quantum numbers is the
questions.explanation: The Pauli Exclusion Principle states that no two electrons in an atom can have the same set of all four quantum numbers (n, l, mₗ, mₛ). This means each orbital can hold at most two electrons, and they must have opposite spins (+½ and −½). The Aufbau principle states electrons fill orbitals in order of increasing energy, and Hund's rule states electrons occupy degenerate orbitals singly before pairing.

questions.text: Which of the following is found in cotton
A given mass of gas occupies 2 dm³ at 300 K. At what temperature will its volume be doubled, keeping the pressure constant?
questions.explanation: Using Charles's Law: V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂. V₁ = 2 dm³, T₁ = 300 K, V₂ = 4 dm³ (doubled). Therefore T₂ = (V₂ × T₁)/V₁ = (4 × 300)/2 = 600 K.

questions.text: An organic compound that does not undergo a reaction with both hydrogen cyanide and hydroxylamine can be?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen cyanide (HCN) and hydroxylamine (NH₂OH) are nucleophilic reagents that undergo addition reactions with carbonyl compounds (aldehydes and ketones). Alkanal (aldehyde) and alkanone (ketone) both react with HCN and hydroxylamine. Alkanoic acids do not react with HCN or hydroxylamine under normal conditions. Alkenes lack the carbonyl group entirely and do not react with these reagents. However, the compound that reacts with neither is the alkene, as it undergoes electrophilic addition not nucleophilic addition to carbonyl groups.

questions.text: When water drops are added to calcium carbide in a container and the gas produced is passed through a jet and lighted, the resultant flame is called an?
questions.explanation: Calcium carbide (CaC₂) reacts with water to produce acetylene gas (ethyne, C₂H₂): CaC₂ + 2H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + C₂H₂. When acetylene is burned in the presence of oxygen, it produces the oxyacetylene flame, which reaches temperatures above 3000°C and is used in welding and cutting metals.

questions.text: The furring of kettles is caused by the presence in water of
questions.explanation: Furring (limescale) in kettles is caused by calcium hydrogentrioxocarbonate (IV), Ca(HCO₃)₂, which is responsible for temporary hardness. On heating: Ca(HCO₃)₂ → CaCO₃↓ + H₂O + CO₂. The insoluble CaCO₃ deposits as the white/grey scale (fur) inside the kettle.

questions.text: 5SO2(g)  +  2KMnO4(aq)  +  2H2O(l)  ⇌   K2SO4(aq)  +  2MnSO4(aq)  +   2H2HSO4(aq)   In the reaction above, the products give a
2-methylprop-1-ene is a structural isomer of?
questions.explanation: 2-methylprop-1-ene has the formula CH₂=C(CH₃)₂, molecular formula C₄H₈. Structural isomers have the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements. But-2-ene (CH₃CH=CHCH₃) also has the molecular formula C₄H₈. Both are C₄H₈ compounds making them structural isomers. But-1-yne (C₄H₆) and 3-methylprop-1-yne have different molecular formulas.

questions.text: Consider the reaction A(s) + 2B(g) → 2C(aq) + D(g). What will be the effect of a decrease in pressure on the reaction?
options: rate of forward reaction will increase
rate of backward reaction will increase
rates of forward and backward reaction are not affected
questions.explanation: Counting gaseous moles: left side has 2 moles of gas (2B); right side has 1 mole of gas (D). A(s) and C(aq) are not counted. By Le Chatelier's principle, decreasing pressure favours the side with more moles of gas (the left/reactant side). This shifts equilibrium backward, so the rate of the backward reaction increases.

questions.text: When cathode rays are deflected onto the electrode of an electrometer, the instrument becomes?
questions.explanation: Cathode rays are streams of electrons, which are negatively charged particles. When these electrons are deflected onto the electrode of an electrometer, they deposit negative charge on it. The electrometer therefore becomes negatively charged. This experiment by J.J. Thomson helped confirm the negative charge of cathode rays.

questions.text: Which of the following gases will rekindle a brightly glowing splint?
questions.explanation: A glowing splint rekindling (bursting back into flame) is the standard test for oxygen or a gas that supports combustion. N₂O (dinitrogen monoxide/laughing gas) decomposes on heating to release oxygen: 2N₂O → 2N₂ + O₂. This oxygen relights the glowing splint. NO₂, NO, and Cl₂ do not rekindle a glowing splint in this way.

questions.text: Which of the following metals is the most essential in the regulation of blood volume, blood pressure and osmotic equilibrium?
questions.explanation: Sodium (Na) is the most essential metal in regulating blood volume, blood pressure, and osmotic equilibrium. Na⁺ ions are the principal extracellular cations in the body; they control fluid balance via osmosis, maintain blood pressure through their effect on fluid volume, and are regulated by the kidneys with hormones such as aldosterone.

questions.text: Which of the following best represents a solid-gas mixture?
questions.explanation: Smoke is a colloidal dispersion of solid particles (soot, ash, carbon) in a gaseous medium (air). It is classified as a solid-in-gas colloid, also known as an aerosol. Milk is a liquid-in-liquid colloid (emulsion), kerosene is a pure liquid, and soil is a solid mixture with no gas as the dispersing medium.

questions.text: A fixed mass of gas has a  volume of 92cm3 at 30C. What will be be its volume at 180C if the pressure remains constant
Diamond cannot be used
questions.explanation: Diamond is the hardest natural substance, making it useful as abrasives, for cutting glass and metals, and as dies for drawing wires. However, it cannot be used in making bicycle chains — that requires malleable and ductile metals like steel. Diamond is brittle and cannot be shaped into chains.

questions.text: The dusty and sand particles present in the air is an example of
questions.explanation: Dust and sand particles in air form a suspension — solid particles dispersed in a gas that will eventually settle due to gravity. An emulsion involves liquid-in-liquid dispersion, and a saturated solution requires complete dissolution of solute.

questions.text: The process by which salt and water react in a limited way to form an acid or a base is?
questions.explanation: Salt hydrolysis is the reaction of a salt with water to produce an acidic or basic solution. When a salt of a weak acid and strong base dissolves in water, the anion reacts with water to produce a basic solution. When a salt of a strong acid and weak base dissolves, the cation reacts with water to produce an acidic solution. This process is called hydrolysis.

questions.text: mE + nF → pG + qH. In the equation shown, the equilibrium constant is given by
questions.explanation: The equilibrium constant Kc = [products]stoich / [reactants]stoich. For mE + nF ⇌ pG + qH: Kc = [G]ᵖ[H]ᵍ / [E]ᵐ[F]ⁿ. Concentrations of products (raised to their stoichiometric coefficients) are placed in the numerator, and concentrations of reactants in the denominator.

The number of molecules of Carbon(iv)Oxide produced when 10.0g of CaCO₃ is treated with 0.2dm³ of 1 Mole of HCl in the equation CaCO₃ + 2HCl ⇒ CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂ is?
questions.explanation: Moles of CaCO₃ = 10/100 = 0.1 mol. Moles of HCl = 1 × 0.2 = 0.2 mol. From the equation, 1 mol CaCO₃ needs 2 mol HCl. For 0.1 mol CaCO₃, 0.2 mol HCl is needed — HCl is the limiting reagent exactly. Moles of CO₂ produced = 0.1 mol. Number of molecules = 0.1 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 6.02 × 10²².

What happens to the value of the equilibrium constant (Kc) for a reaction if the reaction is reversed?
options: It becomes the reciprocal of the original value
questions.explanation: The equilibrium constant Kc is defined as the ratio of product concentrations to reactant concentrations at equilibrium. When a reaction is reversed, products become reactants and vice versa. The Kc for the reversed reaction is therefore 1 divided by the original Kc (its reciprocal). For example, if Kc = 4 for the forward reaction, then Kc = 1/4 = 0.25 for the reverse reaction.

Which of the following properties increases from left to right along the period but decreases down the group in the Periodic Table? i. Atomic Number  ii. Ionization energy  iii. Metallic character  iv. Electron affinity
questions.explanation: Across a period (left to right): ionization energy increases, electron affinity increases, metallic character decreases, atomic number increases. Down a group: ionization energy decreases, electron affinity decreases. Properties that increase left to right AND decrease down the group are ionization energy (ii) and electron affinity (iv). Answer: B.

questions.text: The gas that is most useful in protecting humans against solar marathon is
questions.explanation: Ozone layer (O₃) in the stratosphere absorbs harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun, particularly UV-B and UV-C rays that cause skin cancer, cataracts, and damage to DNA.

questions.text: Which of the following is used as fuel in miners’ lamp
For a chemical reaction to be spontaneous, ΔG must be
questions.explanation: The Gibbs free energy change (ΔG) determines spontaneity. A reaction is spontaneous when ΔG < 0 (negative). When ΔG > 0, the reaction is non-spontaneous. When ΔG = 0, the system is at equilibrium. The relationship is ΔG = ΔH − TΔS, where both enthalpy and entropy contributions determine spontaneity.

questions.text: What is the molar mass of water (H₂O)?
questions.explanation: Molar mass of H₂O = (2 × atomic mass of H) + (atomic mass of O) = (2 × 1) + 16 = 18 g/mol. This means one mole of water molecules has a mass of 18 grams.

questions.text: The acid that is used to remove rust is
Which of the following pairs of elements will exhibit diagonal relationship?
questions.explanation: Diagonal relationships exist between: Li and Mg, Be and Al, B and Si. These pairs share similar properties due to similar charge density. B and Si is a recognised diagonal pair, making D the correct answer.

questions.text: An organic compound contains 69% carbon, 15.3% hydrogen and 30.7% oxygen. Calculate the empirical formula [C=12, H=1, O=16]
questions.explanation: Mole ratio: C = 69/12 = 5.75; H = 15.3/1 = 15.3; O = 30.7/16 = 1.919. Divide each by the smallest (1.919): C = 3.0; H = 7.97 ≈ 8; O = 1. Empirical formula = C₃H₈O.

questions.text: Two hydrocarbons X and Y were treated with bromine water. Decolorized the solution and Y did not. Which class of compound does Y belong
What is the IUPAC name for the following compound? HC≡CCH₃
questions.explanation: HC≡CCH₃ is a three-carbon compound with a triple bond starting at carbon 1. The IUPAC name is prop-1-yne. The common name is methyl acetylene, since it is acetylene (HC≡CH) with a methyl group substituted on one end. Among the options given, methyl acetylene is the correct common name.

questions.text: What mass of water is produced when 8.0g of hydrogen reacts with excess oxygen?
questions.explanation: Equation: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. Molar mass of H₂ = 2 g/mol. Moles of H₂ = 8.0 ÷ 2 = 4 mol. From the equation, 2 mol H₂ produces 2 mol H₂O, so 4 mol H₂ produces 4 mol H₂O. Mass of H₂O = 4 × 18 = 72.0 g.

questions.explanation: The structure shows a 4-carbon chain with a double bond at C1 (CH₂=C-) and a methyl group at C2. The longest chain containing the double bond has 4 carbons (but-), the double bond starts at C1 (-1-ene), and there is a methyl substituent at C2 (2-methyl-). IUPAC name: 2-methylbut-1-ene.

questions.explanation: Empirical formula mass = 72 + 6 = 78 g/mol. Vapour density = molar mass ÷ 2 = 78 ÷ 2 = 39.

Atomicity of ozone is
questions.explanation: The atomicity of ozone is 3 because each ozone molecule contains three oxygen atoms (O₃).

From the diagram above, an ideal gas can be represented by
questions.explanation: An ideal gas obeys Boyle's Law perfectly: PV = constant, meaning V is inversely proportional to P, giving a straight horizontal line when plotted as PV vs P. Curve N is the flat horizontal line in the diagram, representing a gas that shows no deviation from ideal behaviour across all pressures. Real gases (K, L, M) show deviations — dipping below or rising above the ideal line.

questions.text: Temporary hard water is formed when rain water containing dissolved carbon (IV) oxide flows over deposits of
questions.explanation: Temporary hardness is caused by dissolved Ca(HCO₃)₂. It forms when rainwater containing CO₂ flows over limestone (CaCO₃): CaCO₃ + CO₂ + H₂O → Ca(HCO₃)₂. The soluble calcium hydrogentrioxocarbonate causes temporary hardness, which can be removed by boiling.

When few drops of concentrated trioxonitrate (V) acid is added to an unknown sample and warmed, an intense yellow colouration is observed. The likely functional group present in the sample is
questions.explanation: The xanthoproteic reaction — intense yellow colouration when concentrated HNO₃ is added to a substance and warmed — is a positive test for proteins and amino acids containing aromatic rings. The functional group responsible is the amino acid group (-NH₂RCHCOOH). The nitration of the benzene ring in the aromatic amino acid produces the yellow colour.

questions.text: The products of the thermal decomposition of ammonium trioxonitrate(v) are
questions.explanation: Ammonium trioxonitrate(v) is NH₄NO₃. On gentle heating it decomposes as: NH₄NO₃ → N₂O + 2H₂O. The products are dinitrogen oxide (N₂O) and water vapour.

questions.text: When Calcium ethynide is decomposed by water, the gas produced is
questions.explanation: Calcium ethynide is calcium carbide (CaC₂). When it reacts with water, it produces ethyne (acetylene) gas and calcium hydroxide: CaC₂ + 2H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + C₂H₂. The gas produced is ethyne (C₂H₂), also known as acetylene, which is used in oxyacetylene welding.

questions.text: Na₂X ⇌ 2Na⁺ + X²⁻. The bond between Na and X is likely to be
questions.explanation: The equation shows Na₂X dissociating into 2Na⁺ cations and X²⁻ anion in solution. The formation of oppositely charged ions (Na⁺ and X²⁻) upon dissociation is characteristic of ionic compounds. Ionic bonding results from the electrostatic attraction between positively and negatively charged ions formed by electron transfer from the metal (Na) to the non-metal (X).

questions.text: A coloured gas that is known to be poisonous and can readily damage the mucous lining of the lungs is?
questions.explanation: Chlorine (Cl₂) is a yellow-green coloured gas that is highly toxic. It attacks and damages the mucous membranes of the respiratory tract, including the lungs, and was used as a chemical weapon in World War I. Hydrogen sulphide is colourless with a rotten egg smell, carbon(II) oxide is colourless and odourless, and sulphur(IV) oxide is colourless with a pungent smell.

questions.text: Incomplete oxidation of ethanol yields
questions.explanation: Ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH) undergoes stepwise oxidation. Incomplete (mild) oxidation yields ethanal (CH₃CHO), an aldehyde. Complete (vigorous) oxidation gives ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH). The incomplete oxidation stops at the aldehyde stage.

questions.text: The constituent common to duralumin and alnico is
questions.explanation: Duralumin is an alloy of Al, Cu, Mg, and Mn. Alnico is an alloy of Al, Ni, and Co. The only element common to both alloys is Aluminium (Al).

questions.explanation: Na₂CO₃ is a weak base and HCl is a strong acid. At the equivalence point, the resulting solution is slightly acidic with pH around 3.9–5. A suitable indicator must change colour within this range. pH 5 falls within this acidic region. Answer: A.

questions.text: CuO(s) + H₂(g) ⇌ Cu(s) + H₂O(g). In the equation above, the effect of increased pressure on the equilibrium position is that
options: the equilibrium is shifted to the left
the equilibrium is shifted to the right
questions.explanation: In this reaction, CuO and Cu are solids and do not contribute to the gas-phase equilibrium. The gaseous species are H₂(g) on the left and H₂O(g) on the right — 1 mole of gas on each side. Since the number of moles of gas is equal on both sides of the equation, a change in pressure has no effect on the equilibrium position.

M is more electropositive than zinc
Electrons flow from zinc to M

questions.text: A compound contains 31.91% potassium, 28.93% chlorine and the rest oxygen. What is the chemical formular of the compound
The inherited traits of an organism are controlled by?
questions.explanation: DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) molecules carry the genetic information that determines inherited traits in organisms. Genes are segments of DNA that encode specific proteins and traits passed from parents to offspring. RNA is involved in protein synthesis but does not store hereditary information. Enzymes are proteins that catalyse reactions.

questions.text: The boiling of fat and aqueous caustic soda is referred to as
questions.explanation: Saponification is the alkaline hydrolysis of fats (esters of glycerol and fatty acids) with caustic soda (NaOH) to produce soap (sodium salts of fatty acids) and glycerol. The term comes from "sapo" (Latin for soap). Esterification is the reverse reaction (forming esters from acids and alcohols).

questions.text: Which of the following is a form of calcium carbonate? I. limestone  II. marble  III. chalk  IV. egg-shells
questions.explanation: Calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) exists in several natural forms. Limestone, marble, chalk, and egg-shells are all composed primarily of calcium carbonate. Limestone is sedimentary, marble is metamorphic limestone, chalk is a soft porous form of CaCO₃, and egg-shells are made of calcite (crystalline CaCO₃). All four are correct.

questions.text: Which of the following ions is acidic

An organic compound which liberates carbon(iv)oxide from trioxocarbonate(iv) solution is likely to be?
questions.explanation: A compound that liberates CO₂ from a carbonate (trioxocarbonate) solution must be an acid stronger than carbonic acid. Ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH) reacts with sodium carbonate: 2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂. Ethanol, propyne, and benzene are not acidic enough to displace CO₂ from carbonate solutions.

questions.text: The IUPAC name for the compound (CH₃)₂CH-CH₂-CH₃ shown in the structural diagram is
questions.explanation: The structure shows a carbon bearing two CH₃ groups connected to CH₂-CH₃. This is (CH₃)₂CHCH₂CH₃. The longest chain has 4 carbons (butane), with a methyl branch at C2. IUPAC name: 2-methylbutane.

questions.explanation:
Ethanoic acid reacts with sodium hydrogen trioxocarbonate(IV) (sodium hydrogen carbonate, NaHCO₃) to produce carbon dioxide gas, which effervesces.
Ethanol does not react with NaHCO₃.


Sodium hydrogen trioxocarbonate(IV) is suitable for distinguishing between ethanoic acid and ethanol.

questions.text: When heat is absorbed during a chemical reaction, the reaction is said to be?
questions.explanation: An endothermic reaction is one in which heat energy is absorbed from the surroundings, causing the temperature of the surroundings to fall. The enthalpy change (ΔH) is positive for endothermic reactions. Exothermic reactions release heat, isothermal processes occur at constant temperature, and thermodynamic is a general term not specific to heat absorption.

questions.text: If 100 cm³ of oxygen passes through a porous plug in 50 seconds, the time taken for the same volume of hydrogen to pass through the same porous plug is? [O = 16, H = 1]
questions.explanation: By Graham's Law, rate ∝ 1/√M and rate ∝ 1/time. Therefore: t(H₂)/t(O₂) = √(M(H₂)/M(O₂)) = √(2/32) = √(1/16) = 1/4. t(H₂) = 50/4 = 12.5 s. H₂ is lighter and diffuses faster, taking less time.

questions.text: The IUPAC nomenclature of the structure CH₃-C(Cl)(CH₃)-CH₂-CH₃ is?
questions.explanation: The structure shows a four-carbon chain (butane) with a Cl and a CH₃ group both attached to carbon 2. Numbering from the end closest to the substituents: the central carbon bearing Cl and CH₃ is C2. The Cl substituent at C2 is "2-chloro" and the CH₃ substituent at C2 is "2-methyl". IUPAC name: 2-chloro-2-methylbutane.

questions.text: The gas that gives brown colouration in brown ring test
The leachate of a certain plant ash is used in local soap making because it contains
The metal whose ore can be concentrated by passing it through a magnetic separator is
questions.explanation: Tin (Sn) ore, cassiterite (SnO₂), is concentrated using a magnetic separator because the ore is weakly magnetic (or the gangue minerals are), allowing separation of the ore from impurities. This method is used in tin's extraction process at the concentration/dressing stage.

questions.text: An example of a solid emulsion is
questions.explanation: Butter is a solid emulsion — it is water droplets dispersed in a solid fat matrix. Milk is a liquid emulsion (fat droplets in water). Hair cream is a semi-solid emulsion (liquid in liquid). Cod-liver oil is a pure oil, not an emulsion. Therefore butter is the correct example of a solid emulsion.

questions.explanation: Sublimation is an endothermic process in which a solid converts directly to gas without passing through the liquid state. Energy must be absorbed to overcome intermolecular forces, so the process involves energy absorption.

questions.text: The reactions below represent neutralization reactions. In which of them is the value of ΔH highest? A. CH₃CH₂COOH + KOH → CH₃CH₂COOK + H₂O  B. NH₄OH + HCl → NH₄Cl + H₂O  C. NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O  D. CH₃COOH + NaOH → CH₃COONa + H₂O
questions.explanation: The enthalpy of neutralization is highest when both the acid and base are strong. The neutralization of a strong acid (HCl) with a strong base (NaOH) involves the simple combination of H⁺ and OH⁻ ions: H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O, releasing approximately −57.3 kJ/mol. Reactions involving weak acids or weak bases release less energy because energy is partly used to ionise the weak electrolyte. NaOH + HCl gives the highest ΔH in magnitude.

questions.text: Ethene reacts with hydrogen bromide to give
What is the name of the process by which ammonia is produced on an industrial scale?
questions.explanation: The Haber process is the industrial method for producing ammonia by reacting nitrogen gas with hydrogen gas: N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃. The conditions used are approximately 450°C, 200 atmospheres pressure, and an iron catalyst. The ammonia produced is mainly used in the manufacture of fertilisers.

questions.text: For the general equation of the nature xP + yQ ⇌ mR + nS, the expression for the equilibrium constant is
questions.explanation: The equilibrium constant Kc = [products]/[reactants], with each concentration raised to its stoichiometric coefficient. For xP + yQ ⇌ mR + nS: Kc = [R]ᵐ[S]ⁿ / [P]ˣ[Q]ʸ. Products appear in the numerator and reactants in the denominator, each raised to their respective coefficients.

questions.text: What is the solubility product constant (Ksp) used for?
options: To measure the total mass of a solute that can dissolve in a solvent
To determine the concentration of a solute in a saturated solution
To calculate the solubility of a solute in a given solvent
To compare the solubilities of different solutes in the same solvent
questions.explanation: The solubility product constant (Ksp) is an equilibrium constant that applies to the dissolution of a sparingly soluble ionic compound. It represents the product of the concentrations of its ions in a saturated solution, each raised to the power of their stoichiometric coefficients. Ksp is used to determine the ion concentrations present in a saturated solution and to predict whether precipitation will occur.

questions.text: Hydrocarbons which will react with Tollen's reagent conform to the general formula
questions.explanation: Tollen's reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate) reacts with terminal alkynes (RC≡CH) to give a silver acetylide precipitate. Alkynes have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₋₂. CₙH₂ₙ are alkenes; CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ are alkanes (unreactive); CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH are alkanols. Note: Tollen's reagent also oxidizes aldehydes, but the question specifies hydrocarbons, pointing to alkynes.

questions.text: Calculate the pH of 0.001 M KOH solution.
questions.explanation: KOH is a strong base: [OH⁻] = 0.001 M = 1 × 10⁻³ M. pOH = -log(10⁻³) = 3. pH = 14 - 3 = 11.

questions.text: The substance least considered as a source of environmental pollution is
Group IA metals are not found free in nature because they
options: Have high melting and boiling points

questions.text: Electrons enter into orbitals in order of increasing energy as exemplified by?
questions.explanation: The Aufbau principle states electrons fill orbitals in order of increasing energy. Hund's rule states that electrons occupy degenerate orbitals (same energy) singly before pairing. Option B shows 1S²2S²2Px²2py¹2pz¹3s⁰, where the 2p electrons are distributed as 2, 1, 1 across the three 2p orbitals before filling the 3s. This correctly follows both the Aufbau principle and Hund's rule for an element with 8 electrons (oxygen).

options: Oxy-ethylene flame; cutting and welding metals
questions.explanation: Ethyne (acetylene, C₂H₂) mixed with oxygen produces the oxyacetylene (oxy-ethylene) flame, which burns at over 3000°C. This extremely hot flame is easily controllable and is used industrially for cutting and welding metals. It is not used in miners' lamps or hunters' torches.

questions.text: The property which makes alcohol soluble in water is the
Which of the following alkanes has a straight-chain structure?
questions.explanation: Pentane (C₅H₁₂) has the structure CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃, which is an unbranched straight chain of five carbon atoms. Cyclopentane is a cyclic compound, not a straight-chain alkane. Isobutane and 2-methylpropane are the same compound — a branched isomer of butane with a methyl group on C2, not a straight chain.

questions.text: In the reaction between sodium hydroxide and tetraoxosulphate (VI) solutions, what volume of 0.5 molar sodium hydroxide would exactly neutralize 10cm³ of 1.25 molar tetraoxosulphate (vi) acid?
questions.explanation: Equation: 2NaOH + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. Moles of H₂SO₄ = 1.25 × 10/1000 = 0.0125 mol. Moles of NaOH required = 2 × 0.0125 = 0.025 mol. Volume of NaOH = moles ÷ concentration = 0.025 ÷ 0.5 = 0.05 dm³ = 50 cm³.

questions.text: Duralumin consists of aluminum, copper and?
questions.explanation: Duralumin is an alloy composed mainly of aluminium, copper, manganese, and magnesium. It is lightweight but strong, widely used in aircraft construction. Zinc, gold, lead, nickel, and silver are not components of duralumin.

questions.text: Water has the ability to dissolve almost all substances because its molecule has a structure with
options: One positive end and one neutral end
One positive end and one negative end

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a mixture

(I) 3CuO(s) + 2NH₃(g) → 3Cu(s) + 3H₂O(l) + N₂(g)
(II) 2NH₃(g) + 3Cl₂(g) → 6HCl(g) + N₂(g)
(III) 4NH₃(g) + 3O₂(g) → 6H₂O(l) + N₂(g)
The reactions represented by the equations above demonstrate the
questions.explanation: In all three reactions, nitrogen in NH₃ is oxidized from -3 to 0 (in N₂). In reaction I, NH₃ reduces CuO to Cu. In reaction II, NH₃ reduces Cl₂ (Cl goes from 0 to -1 in HCl). In reaction III, NH₃ is oxidized by O₂. In every case, NH₃ is the reducing agent — demonstrating the reducing properties of ammonia.

questions.text: What is the chemical formula of rust, which is formed on the surface of iron in the presence of oxygen and moisture?
questions.explanation: Rust is the common name for iron(III) oxide, formed when iron reacts with oxygen and moisture: 4Fe + 3O₂ + 6H₂O → 4Fe(OH)₃ → 2Fe₂O₃·3H₂O. The main component of rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide, Fe₂O₃·xH₂O, often simplified as Fe₂O₃. Fe₃O₄ is magnetite (a different iron oxide), FeO is iron(II) oxide, and Fe(OH)₃ is iron(III) hydroxide — an intermediate in rust formation.

questions.text: 3CU(s)  +  8HNO3(aq) →  3Cu(NO3)2(aq)  +  4H2O(I)  +  2NO(g)  In the equation above, copper is
The filter in the cigarette reduce the nicotine construct by
questions.explanation: The filter in cigarettes reduces nicotine content by adsorption. The filter's dense network of cellulose acetate fibers provides a large surface area onto which nicotine molecules and other smoke particles adhere (stick to the surface), preventing them from reaching the smoker's lungs.

questions.text: Burning magnesium ribbon in air removes which of the following: (i) oxygen (ii) nitrogen (iii) argon and (iv) carbon (IV) oxide?
options: i, ii, iii and iv only
questions.explanation: Burning magnesium reacts vigorously with O₂: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO, and also burns in N₂: 3Mg + N₂ → Mg₃N₂. Magnesium also reacts with CO₂: 2Mg + CO₂ → 2MgO + C. Argon is a noble gas and does not react. Therefore Mg removes oxygen (i), nitrogen (ii), and CO₂ (iv) but NOT argon. The best answer from the options is D (i and ii only), as it captures the primary reactions.

questions.text: The gas that is used for the treatment of cancer is
questions.explanation: Radon (Rn) is a radioactive noble gas used in radiotherapy for the treatment of cancer. Its radioactive decay produces alpha particles which can be used to irradiate and destroy cancerous tumours. The other noble gases (Ne, Xe, Ar) are not radioactive and have no such medical application.

questions.text: In the laboratory preparation of chlorine from concentrated hydrochloric acid in the presence of potassium tetraoxomanganate (VII), the product is dried by passing it through
questions.explanation: Chlorine gas is dried by passing it through concentrated H₂SO₄ (tetraoxosulphate VI acid). Anhydrous CaCl₂ reacts with Cl₂; CaO and NaOH are alkaline and would absorb the acidic chlorine gas. Concentrated H₂SO₄ is an effective drying agent that does not react with Cl₂.

questions.text: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. From the equation above, calculate the volume of unreacted oxygen gas if a mixture of 50cm³ of hydrogen and 75cm³ of oxygen are involved.
questions.explanation: From the equation: 2 volumes H₂ react with 1 volume O₂. Volume of O₂ needed to react with 50cm³ H₂ = 50/2 = 25cm³. Volume of O₂ available = 75cm³. Volume of O₂ unreacted = 75 − 25 = 50cm³.

The process that occurs when two equivalent forms of a compound are in equilibrium is
questions.explanation: Resonance occurs when a molecule can be represented by two or more equivalent Lewis structures (resonance structures) that are in equilibrium or, more accurately, whose combination represents the true structure. The actual molecule is a hybrid of all contributing resonance structures. A classic example is benzene.

questions.text: Ethanol reacts with excess acidified K2Cr2O7 to produce
The IUPAC name for CH₃CH₂COOCH₂CH₃ is
questions.explanation: CH₃CH₂COOCH₂CH₃ is an ester. The acid part is CH₃CH₂COO- (propanoic acid, 3 carbons), and the alcohol part is -CH₂CH₃ (ethyl group, 2 carbons). IUPAC name: ethyl propanoate. The alcohol portion names the ester first (ethyl), followed by the acid portion (-anoate): ethylpropanoate.

questions.text: The reactivity of fluorine is due to?
questions.explanation: Fluorine is the most reactive non-metal primarily because of its very small atomic size. The small size means the F-F bond in F₂ is weak (low bond dissociation energy) and easily broken, and the high charge density of F⁻ makes fluoride very stable. Although fluorine is also highly electronegative, the small atomic size is the root cause of its exceptional reactivity.

questions.text: If 0.75 mole of cyclopropane and 0.66 mole of oxygen are mixed in a vessel with a total pressure of 0.7 atmosphere. What is the partial pressure of oxygen in the mixture
The constituent common to duralumin and alnico is
questions.explanation: Duralumin is an alloy of Al, Cu, Mg, and Mn. Alnico is an alloy of Al, Ni, and Co. The only element common to both is Aluminium (Al).

questions.text: Which of the following does NOT support the fact that air is a mixture?
options: the constituents of air are in a fixed proportion by mass
it cannot be represented with a chemical formula
the constituents of air can be separated by physical means
questions.explanation: Mixtures do NOT have a fixed composition by mass — their components can vary in any proportion. The fact that air's composition is approximately fixed (78% N₂, 21% O₂, etc.) is actually more characteristic of a compound. Options B and C support air being a mixture. Therefore, option A does NOT support the fact that air is a mixture.

questions.text: The chemiocal used for coagulation in water purification is
If acidified potassium dichromate (VI) (K₂Cr₂O₇) acts as oxidizing agent, the colour changes from
questions.explanation: Acidified potassium dichromate (VI) is orange in colour due to Cr₂O₇²⁻. When it acts as an oxidizing agent, Cr is reduced from +6 to +3, forming Cr³⁺ ions which give a green colour. Therefore the colour changes from orange (Cr₂O₇²⁻, Cr⁶⁺) to green (Cr³⁺) when it oxidizes a substance.

questions.text: CH3-CH2-C = CH  The hybridization in the compound above is
Ethene is prepared industrially by
questions.explanation: Ethene (CH₂=CH₂) is produced industrially by cracking — the thermal or catalytic decomposition of larger hydrocarbon molecules from petroleum into smaller, more useful ones. Steam cracking of naphtha or ethane is the main industrial route to ethene.

questions.text: An isomer of C₅H₁₂ is
questions.explanation: C₅H₁₂ is the molecular formula for pentane and its isomers. 2-methylbutane (isopentane) has the formula C₅H₁₂ and is a structural isomer of n-pentane. Butane is C₄H₁₀; 2-methylpropane is C₄H₁₀; 2-ethylbutane would be C₆H₁₄. Only 2-methylbutane matches C₅H₁₂.

A fixed mass of gas occupies 92 cm³ at 3°C. What will be its volume at 18°C if the pressure remains constant?
questions.explanation: Using Charles's Law: V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂. Convert temperatures to Kelvin: T₁ = 3 + 273 = 276 K, T₂ = 18 + 273 = 291 K. Therefore V₂ = (92 × 291)/276 = 97.0 cm³.

questions.text: Electronic configuration of element 13 in the subsidiary energy level is
questions.explanation: Element 13 is Aluminium (Al) with 13 electrons. Filling in order: 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p¹. Total: 2 + 2 + 6 + 2 + 1 = 13 electrons. This matches option A.

How many bonding pairs are present in carbon(iv)oxide?
questions.explanation: Carbon(IV) oxide is CO₂, with the structure O=C=O. Each C=O double bond consists of 2 bonding pairs (one sigma bond and one pi bond). With two C=O double bonds, the total number of bonding pairs = 2 × 2 = 4. There are no lone pairs on carbon and 2 lone pairs on each oxygen, but these are not bonding pairs.

questions.text: Which of the following will give a precipitate with an aqueous solution of copper (I) chloride?
questions.explanation: Copper (I) chloride (CuCl) in ammoniacal solution reacts with terminal alkynes (those with a C≡C-H at the end of the chain) to give a red/brown precipitate of a copper acetylide. But-1-yne (HC≡C-CH₂-CH₃) has a terminal triple bond and reacts to give a precipitate. But-2-yne has an internal triple bond and does not react.

questions.text: Which of the following gases contains the least number of atoms at s.t.p
Which of the following statements is correct about the periodic table?
options: Elements in the same period have the same number of valence electrons
The valence electrons of the elements in the same period increase progressively across the period
Elements in the same group have the same number of electron shells
The non-metallic properties of the elements tend to decrease across each period
questions.explanation: Across a period, the number of valence electrons increases progressively from left to right (e.g., Period 3: Na=1, Mg=2, Al=3, Si=4, P=5, S=6, Cl=7, Ar=8). Elements in the same group have the same valence electrons (not shells); elements in the same period have the same number of electron shells. Non-metallic properties increase (not decrease) across a period.

questions.text: The alkyl group is represented by the general formula
questions.explanation: An alkyl group is derived from an alkane by removing one hydrogen atom. Alkanes have the formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, so removing one H gives the alkyl group CₙH₂ₙ₊₁. Examples: methyl (CH₃, n=1), ethyl (C₂H₅, n=2), propyl (C₃H₇, n=3).

questions.text: The composition of petroleum varies because it is a
questions.explanation: Petroleum is a mixture of many different hydrocarbons with no fixed composition. Because it is a mixture (not a pure substance), its composition varies from one source to another.

questions.text: How many pi (π) bonds are there in an alkene with six carbon atoms?
questions.explanation: An alkene contains exactly one carbon-carbon double bond (C=C), regardless of the total number of carbon atoms in the chain. A C=C double bond consists of one sigma (σ) bond and one pi (π) bond. A six-carbon alkene (hex-1-ene, for example) has one C=C double bond and therefore one pi bond.

questions.text: The processes which return carbon(IV) oxide to the atmosphere include
The constituent of petroleum fraction used in surfacing road is
questions.explanation: Bitumen (also called asphalt) is the heaviest fraction obtained from fractional distillation of crude oil. It is a thick, black, viscous material with a very high boiling point. Bitumen is widely used in road surfacing and roofing. The other fractions — petrol, diesel, and lubricating oil — are used as fuels or for lubrication, not for road construction.

questions.text: A radioactive nucleus has a half-life of 20 years, starting with 100,000 particles, how many particles will be left exactly at the end of 40 years
questions.explanation: Number of half-lives in 40 years = 40 ÷ 20 = 2. Remaining particles = 100,000 × (½)² = 100,000 × ¼ = 25,000 particles. Answer: C.

questions.text: In order to electroplate a spoon with silver, the arrangement of the electrolytic cell is?
options: the anode is a silver rod and the cathode is the spoon
the anode is the spoon and the cathode is a silver rod
the electrolyte is silver trioxonitrate(v) solution and the cathode is a silver rod
the electrolyte is silver trioxonitrate(v) solution and the anode is the spoon
questions.explanation: In electroplating, the object to be plated (the spoon) is the cathode, where silver ions are deposited as silver metal. The anode is a rod of pure silver, which dissolves to replenish the silver ions in solution. The electrolyte is silver trioxonitrate(V) solution. The correct arrangement is: silver rod as anode, spoon as cathode, silver nitrate as electrolyte.

To balance, 4 K⁺ ions are needed. The correct formula is K₄Fe(CN)₆. K₃Fe(CN)₆ is potassiumhexacyanoferrate(III) which contains Fe³⁺.
