Water vapour in the air around loses some of its energy to the bottle
Water vapour in the air around the bottle gains some energy from the bottle

questions.text: The empirical mass of C₆H₁₂O₆ is [H = 1, C = 12, O = 16]
questions.explanation: The empirical formula is found by simplifying the ratio C:H:O = 6:12:6 = 1:2:1, giving CH₂O. Empirical mass = 12 + 2(1) + 16 = 30 g/mol.

questions.text: The reaction above is
When a crystal was added to the clear solution of its salt, the crystal did not dissolve and the solution remained unchanged. This showed that the solution was
The major product when 2-methylpropene reacts with HCl is
questions.explanation: By Markovnikov's rule, H⁺ adds to the less substituted carbon (=CH₂) and Cl⁻ adds to the more substituted carbon (=C(CH₃)₂), forming the more stable tertiary carbocation intermediate. The major product is 2-chloro-2-methylpropane.

questions.text: Deliquescent substances are also?
questions.explanation: Deliquescent substances absorb moisture from the atmosphere to the extent of dissolving in it. Hygroscopic substances also absorb moisture from the atmosphere. Deliquescent substances are a specific category of hygroscopic substances, since absorbing moisture until dissolution is an extreme form of hygroscopicity. All deliquescent substances are hygroscopic, but not all hygroscopic substances are deliquescent.

questions.text: What volume of oxygen is produced from the decomposition of 2 moles of KClO3 at s.t.p   [Molar volume of a gas at s.t.p = 22.4 dm3]
In which of the following will hydrogen form an ionic compound?
questions.explanation: Ionic compounds form between elements with large differences in electronegativity. In NaH (sodium hydride), sodium (a very electropositive metal) donates its electron to hydrogen, forming Na⁺ and H⁻ ions. This is an ionic compound. HCl, NH₃, and CH₄ are all covalent compounds where hydrogen shares electrons rather than forming ions.

questions.text: Which of these radioactive elements is commonly used as a nuclear fuel?
questions.explanation: Uranium (specifically U-235) is the most commonly used nuclear fuel. Its nucleus undergoes fission when struck by a slow neutron, releasing enormous energy and additional neutrons that sustain a chain reaction in nuclear reactors.

questions.text: Helium is used in observation balloons because it is?
questions.explanation: Helium is the second lightest element, making it ideal for lifting balloons. It is also a noble gas and completely non-combustible, making it much safer than hydrogen (which is equally light but highly flammable). These two properties, lightness and non-combustibility, make helium the preferred gas for observation balloons.

questions.text: A concentrated solution containing H+, Cu2+, OH- and Cl- was electrolyzed using platinum electrodes. The ion that will be discharged at the cathode is
Which of the following is used to power steam engines?
questions.explanation: Coal is the fuel used to power steam engines. It is burned in the furnace of the steam engine to heat water and produce steam, which drives the pistons or turbines. Coal was the primary fuel of the Industrial Revolution and early locomotives. Lubricating oil reduces friction; bitumen is used for road surfacing; diesel powers internal combustion engines.

questions.text: The residual solids from the fractional distillation of petroleum are used as
options: Raw materials for the cracking process

questions.text: What is the common name for ethanoic acid?
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH) is the IUPAC name for the compound commonly known as acetic acid. It is the main component of vinegar and has a characteristic sharp smell. Formic acid is methanoic acid (HCOOH), propionic acid is propanoic acid (CH₃CH₂COOH), and butyric acid is butanoic acid (CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH).

questions.text: Which of the following represents the kind of bonding present in ammonium chloride?
questions.explanation: NH₄Cl contains both ionic and covalent bonding. Within the NH₄⁺ ion, there are three ordinary N-H covalent bonds and one dative covalent bond (from NH₃ + H⁺). Between NH₄⁺ and Cl⁻, the bonding is ionic (electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions). So NH₄Cl has both ionic and covalent bonding.

questions.text: Due to the high reactivity of sodium, it is usually stored under
questions.explanation: Sodium is stored under paraffin oil (kerosene/mineral oil) to prevent it from reacting with oxygen and moisture in the air. Paraffin is a non-polar, unreactive liquid that forms a protective layer around the sodium. Water would react explosively with sodium; mercury would form an amalgam; phenol would react with sodium.

questions.text: The condition required for corrosion to take place is the presence of
options: Water and Carbon (IV) oxide and Oxygen
questions.explanation: Corrosion (rusting of iron) requires both water and oxygen. Water acts as the electrolyte enabling electron transfer, while oxygen acts as the oxidizing agent. CO₂ is not an essential requirement for basic corrosion to occur.

questions.text: Stainless steel is used for making
In the experiment shown (solid ammonium chloride heated at 350°C, with porous asbestos plug and damp neutral litmus paper at the far end), the litmus paper will initially
questions.explanation: NH₄Cl sublimes on heating and dissociates: NH₄Cl(s) → NH₃(g) + HCl(g). The porous asbestos plug separates the gases — lighter NH₃ diffuses faster and reaches the litmus paper first (Graham's Law). NH₃ is alkaline and turns the damp neutral litmus paper blue initially. Later, HCl may turn it red.

questions.text: Which of the following is a primary constituent of crude oil?
questions.explanation: Crude oil is a complex mixture of hydrocarbons. Heptane (C₇H₁₆) is a significant and representative primary constituent of crude oil, used as a reference compound in the octane rating scale (heptane = 0 octane rating). Pentane is also present in crude oil but heptane is more commonly cited as a primary constituent. Ethanol is not a constituent of crude oil, and methane is the main component of natural gas rather than crude oil.

questions.text: Which of the following acts as both a reducing and an oxidizing agent
What is the chemical name for the compound CuCO₃?
questions.explanation: In CuCO₃, the carbonate ion CO₃²⁻ has a charge of 2−. For the compound to be electrically neutral, copper must have a charge of 2+. A copper ion with a 2+ charge is designated copper(II). The correct chemical name is therefore copper(II) carbonate.

questions.text: Permanent hardness of water can be removed by
What is Faraday's constant?
questions.explanation: Faraday's constant (F) is the electric charge carried by one mole of electrons, equal to 96,485 coulombs per mole (approximately 96,500 C/mol). It is used in electrochemistry calculations relating the amount of substance deposited or dissolved at an electrode to the quantity of electricity passed. 6.022 × 10²³ is Avogadro's number, 3.00 × 10⁸ m/s is the speed of light, and 9.81 m/s² is gravitational acceleration.

questions.text: A compound contains 40.0% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen and 53.3% oxygen. If the molar mass of the compound is 180, find the molecular formula  [H = 1, C = 12, O = 16]
Benzene reacts with hydrogen in the presence of nickel catalyst at 1800C to give
What is the empirical formula of a compound containing 40.00% carbon, 6.67% hydrogen, and 53.33% oxygen by mass?
questions.explanation: Mole ratio: C = 40.00/12 = 3.33; H = 6.67/1 = 6.67; O = 53.33/16 = 3.33. Divide by smallest (3.33): C = 1; H = 2; O = 1. Empirical formula = CH₂O.

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct order of increasing electronegativity?
questions.explanation: Electronegativity increases across a period from left to right. In Period 2: C (2.5) < N (3.0) < O (3.5) < F (4.0). Fluorine is the most electronegative element on the periodic table. The correct order of increasing electronegativity is C < N < O < F.

questions.text: Pure solvents are obtained by
The dehydration of CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH will give?
questions.explanation: Dehydration of an alcohol removes water (H₂O) to form an alkene. CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH (butan-1-ol) loses -OH and an adjacent -H to form a C=C double bond. The major product by Zaitsev's rule is the more substituted alkene: CH₃CH=CHCH₃ (but-2-ene). The double bond forms between C2 and C3, giving the more stable internal alkene.

questions.text: Suitable reagents for the laboratory preparation of nitrogen are
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is prepared in the laboratory by heating a mixture of sodium dioxonitrate (III) (sodium nitrite, NaNO₂) and ammonium chloride (NH₄Cl): NaNO₂ + NH₄Cl → NaCl + 2H₂O + N₂↑. The reaction produces pure nitrogen gas. Sodium trioxonitrate (V) (NaNO₃) is used differently and does not give N₂ in this way.

questions.text: NH₃(g) + HCl(s) → NH₄Cl(s). The entropy change in the system above is
questions.explanation: In this reaction, a gas (NH₃) and a solid (HCl) combine to form a solid (NH₄Cl). The disappearance of the gaseous phase results in a large decrease in disorder. Since the number of gaseous moles decreases from 1 to 0, entropy decreases, giving a negative entropy change (ΔS < 0).

questions.text: The reaction of halogens with alkanes in the presence of sunlight is an example of
questions.explanation: When halogens react with alkanes in the presence of sunlight (UV light), a hydrogen atom in the alkane is replaced (substituted) by a halogen atom via a free radical mechanism. This is free radical substitution. For example: CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl. Addition reactions occur with alkenes, not alkanes.

questions.text: Ethanol is soluble in water due to the presence of a
questions.explanation: Ethanol (C₂H₅OH) is soluble in water because of its hydroxyl group (-OH), which forms hydrogen bonds with water molecules. The -OH group is polar and interacts strongly with the polar water molecules, allowing ethanol to mix with water in all proportions.

questions.text: The reactions involving simultaneous oxidation and reduction are called?
questions.explanation: Redox reactions are chemical reactions in which oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously. One species loses electrons (is oxidised) while another gains those electrons (is reduced). The term redox is a combination of reduction and oxidation. These reactions include combustion, rusting, electrochemical cells, and many biological processes.

questions.text: A balanced chemical equation obeys the law of
questions.explanation: A balanced chemical equation ensures that the number of atoms of each element is equal on both sides of the equation, in accordance with the Law of Conservation of Mass (Lavoisier's Law): matter is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction. Balancing an equation is the practical application of this fundamental law.

questions.text: A chemical reaction in which the hydration energy is greater than the lattice energy is referred to as
questions.explanation: When hydration energy exceeds lattice energy, more energy is released during hydration than is absorbed in breaking the lattice. The net result is a release of energy to the surroundings, making the dissolution process exothermic. Examples include dissolving NaOH or H₂SO₄ in water.

questions.text: Which of the following is a set of neutral oxides?
questions.explanation: Neutral oxides do not react with acids or bases to form salts. N₂O (nitrous oxide), H₂O (water), and CO (carbon monoxide) are all neutral oxides. SO₂ is acidic; Na₂O is basic; ZnO is amphoteric; SO₃ is acidic; NO can behave as a neutral oxide in some contexts but it is debated. Option A (N₂O, H₂O, CO) is the most consistent set of neutral oxides.

options: Increasing the temperature of the system
Increasing the pressure of the system
The addition of a catalyst to the system
Increasing the surface area of the vessel

ZnO(s) + CO (g) → Zn(s) + CO2 (g).
Cu₂S(g) + O₂(g) → 2Cu + SO₂(g). What is the change in the oxidation number of copper in the reaction?
questions.explanation: In Cu₂S, S has oxidation number -2, so each Cu must be +1 (since 2(+1) + (-2) = 0). In the product Cu, copper is in its elemental state with oxidation number 0. Therefore copper changes from +1 (in Cu₂S) to 0 (in Cu) — this is a reduction.

questions.text: C(s) + 2S (g)  → CS2 (g)      Δ H = +89kJ mol-1. The chemical equation above implies that
options: Each of carbon and sulphur has 89kJ of energy
Both carbon and sulphur contribute 89kJ of energy

questions.text: The following is not a water pollutant?
questions.explanation: Oxygen gas is naturally present in water and is essential for aquatic life. Warm water effluent, inorganic fertilizers (cause eutrophication), and biodegradable waste (depletes dissolved oxygen) are all recognised water pollutants. Oxygen is not a pollutant.

questions.text: The most abundant rare gas in the atmosphere is?
questions.explanation: Argon (Ar) is the most abundant noble (rare) gas in the atmosphere, making up approximately 0.93% of dry air by volume. It is the third most abundant gas in the atmosphere after nitrogen and oxygen. Helium, neon, and xenon are present in much smaller quantities.

questions.text: To obtain pure carbon(ii)oxide from its mixture with carbon(iv)oxide, the mixture should be?
questions.explanation: Carbon(iv)oxide (CO₂) is an acidic gas that reacts with concentrated NaOH solution: CO₂ + 2NaOH → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O. Bubbling the mixture through conc NaOH absorbs the CO₂ completely while carbon(ii)oxide (CO) is unaffected and passes through, yielding pure CO. Water absorbs CO₂ only partially, while conc H₂SO₄ is a drying agent and does not remove CO₂.

questions.text: When a solid substance disappears completely as a gas on heating, the substance is said to have undergone?
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the direct change of state from solid to gas without passing through the liquid phase. When a solid disappears completely as a gas on heating without melting first, it has sublimed. Examples include iodine, dry ice (solid CO₂), and ammonium chloride.

questions.text: Calculate the total purchase of a business from the given information, cash purchases ₦3,000; payments to creditors ₦53,000; creditors at the beginning ₦4,000; creditors at the end ₦2,000
questions.explanation:
Formula:
Total Purchases = Cash Purchases + Credit Purchases
Finding Credit Purchases:
Credit Purchases = Payments to Creditors + Closing Creditors - Opening Creditors
Calculation:

Cash Purchases = 3,000
Payments to Creditors = 53,000
Opening Creditors = 4,000
Closing Creditors = 2,000

Credit Purchases = 53,000 + 2,000 - 4,000 = 51,000
Total Purchases:
Total Purchases = Cash Purchases + Credit Purchases
Total Purchases = 3,000 + 51,000 = 54,000
The total purchases of the business amount to ₦54,000

questions.text: Didi Ltd offered 10,000 ordinary shares of ₦1.50 each at a discount of 2% which were fully subscribed. With regard to the offer above?

the value of shares in the capital account will be lowered by 2%
the company incurs a loss to the tune of 2% of the offer
each of the subscribers loses 2% of investment
questions.explanation:
The shares have a nominal value of ₦1.50, so on 10,000 shares the full par amount would be ₦15,000.

At a 2% discount, subscribers actually pay only 98% of par, i.e. ₦1.50 × 0.98 = ₦1.47 per share, so total cash received is ₦14,700.

The “missing” ₦300 (₂₀₀₀ × ₦0.03) is debited to a “Discount on Issue of Shares” account, effectively a capital loss to the company.

Thus the company forgoes 2% of the issue price, incurring that amount as a loss on the share issue.

questions.explanation:
To find Segun Ojo’s capital at 1 Jan 2014, take all assets less all liabilities at that date:

Opening assets

Cash in hand: ₦ ⁠850

Debtors: ₦ 15 500

Stock: ₦ 18 000

Fittings: ₦ ⁠9 000
Total assets = 850 + 15 500 + 18 000 + 9 000 = ₦ 43 350

Opening liabilities

Bank overdraft: ₦ ⁠3 500

questions.explanation:
When goodwill is not retained in the business, it means the goodwill account is written off immediately after being created. This involves a two-step process:
Step 1: Create goodwill

Debit: Goodwill Account
Credit: Partners' Capital Accounts (in profit-sharing ratio)

Step 2: Write off goodwill (since it's not retained)

Debit: Partners' Capital Accounts (in new profit-sharing ratio)
Credit: Goodwill Account

The net effect in the new partners' books is:

Debit: Partners' Capital Account
Credit: Goodwill Account

This represents the partners absorbing the goodwill write-off through their capital accounts rather than keeping it as an asset on the books.

questions.text: At the end of a financial period, the trading profit and loss account of a company showed a profit of ₦120,000. Error 1: Revenue of ₦12,000 was recorded as expenses
Error 2: Expenses of ₦4,000 were recorded as revenue

Analysis of errors:
Error 1: Revenue ₦12,000 recorded as expenses

This reduced profit by ₦24,000 (₦12,000 revenue not added + ₦12,000 wrongly deducted as expenses)
Correction: Add back ₦24,000

Error 2: Expenses ₦4,000 recorded as revenue

questions.text: In a period of inflation, which of the following method normally gives a lower closing stock value?
questions.explanation:
LIFO (Last In, First Out) assumes that the most recently purchased (and therefore most expensive) items are sold first. This means:

The newer, higher-priced inventory gets matched against sales revenue
The older, lower-priced inventory remains in closing stock
This results in a lower closing stock value on the balance sheet

In contrast:

FIFO would show higher closing stock values (newer, expensive items remain)
Simple average and periodic simple average would show moderate values between FIFO and LIFO

LIFO is often preferred during inflation because it:

Matches current costs against current revenues (better income statement matching)
Results in lower reported profits (and thus lower taxes)
Shows more conservative inventory values

So LIFO typically gives the lowest closing stock valuation during inflationary periods.

questions.text:
Mamza ₦igeria Limited issued 20 000 ordinary shares of ₦1.50 per share on 2nd July 2002.
1500 ordinary shares were fully subscribed for and their monies received as below:

On allotment ...........................₦0.20
First call (including premium of ₦0.50)..₦0.70

The last and final call was yet to be made.

What is the balance of the ordinary share capital account after the first call was received?
questions.explanation:
Given Information:

20,000 ordinary shares issued at ₦1.50 per share
1,500 ordinary shares were fully subscribed
Payment schedule:

On application: ₦0.40
On allotment: ₦0.20
First call (including premium of ₦0.50): ₦0.70



Step 1: Determine the nominal value per share
Total payment per share = ₦0.40 + ₦0.20 + ₦0.70 = ₦1.30
Since the issue price is ₦1.50 and there's a premium of ₦0.50 in the first call, the nominal value per share = ₦1.50 - ₦0.50 = ₦1.00
Step 2: Calculate amounts received by stage

Application: 1,500 shares × ₦0.40 = ₦600
Allotment: 1,500 shares × ₦0.20 = ₦300
First call: 1,500 shares × ₦0.70 = ₦1,050

Step 3: Determine what goes to Ordinary Share Capital Account
The Ordinary Share Capital Account only records the nominal value, not the premium.
From the first call of ₦0.70:

Premium portion: ₦0.50 (goes to Share Premium Account)
Nominal value portion: ₦0.70 - ₦0.50 = ₦0.20 (goes to Share Capital Account)

Step 4: Calculate total in Ordinary Share Capital Account

From application: 1,500 × ₦0.40 = ₦600
From allotment: 1,500 × ₦0.20 = ₦300
From first call (nominal portion): 1,500 × ₦0.20 = ₦300

Total in Ordinary Share Capital Account = ₦600 + ₦300 + ₦300 = ₦1,200

questions.explanation:
The acid test ratio (quick ratio) measures a company's ability to pay short-term debts using liquid assets.
Formula:

Calculation:

Current Assets = Stock + Debtors + Cash = ₦40,000 + ₦6,000 + ₦8,000 = ₦54,000
Quick Assets = Current Assets - Stock = ₦54,000 - ₦40,000 = ₦14,000
Current Liabilities = Creditors + Accrued wages = ₦9,000 + ₦5,000 = ₦14,000

Acid Test Ratio = ₦14,000 ÷ ₦14,000 = 1:1
This means the company has exactly enough liquid assets to cover its current liabilities.

The ₦6,000 subscription received for next year is a current liability.


When an organization receives money for subscriptions that relate to the following year, it creates an obligation to provide services in the future. This is known as "unearned revenue" or "deferred income."

The organization has received cash (₦6,000)
But it has not yet provided the service/benefit for next year
Therefore, it owes a service to the subscribers
This creates a liability that must be settled by providing the service next year
Since it will be settled within one year, it's a current liability

This amount would typically be shown on the balance sheet as "Subscriptions Received in Advance" or "Unearned Subscription Income" under current liabilities.
Next year, when the service period begins, this liability will be transferred to subscription income in the profit and loss account.

questions.text: On Ist January, 1993, lobo Company purchased equipment for ₦18,000. it uses straight-line depreciation with an estimates eight-year useful life and a ₦2,000 salvage value. On 31st December, 1996, it sells the equipment for ₦8000. In recording this sales, it should reflect?

To find the gain or loss on sale of equipment, calculate the book value at the time of sale and compare it to the selling price.
Given information:

Purchase date: January 1, 1993
Cost: ₦18,000
Useful life: 8 years
Salvage value: ₦2,000
Sale date: December 31, 1996
Selling price: ₦8,000

Step 1: Calculate annual depreciation
Annual depreciation = (Cost - Salvage value) ÷ Useful life
Annual depreciation = (₦18,000 - ₦2,000) ÷ 8 years = ₦2,000 per year
Step 2: Calculate accumulated depreciation by December 31, 1996
Period of use: January 1, 1993 to December 31, 1996 = 4 years

Book value = Cost - Accumulated depreciation
Book value = ₦18,000 - ₦8,000 = ₦10,000

Loss on sale = Book value - Selling price
Loss on sale = ₦10,000 - ₦8,000 = ₦2,000 loss

Using the information provided: total current assets ₦2,000, total fixed assets ₦4,000, current liabilities ₦1,200, drawings ₦200, and long term loan ₦2,000, calculate the capital of the business.
questions.explanation:
To calculate capital, use the accounting equation:
Assets = Liabilities + Capital
First, calculate total assets and total liabilities:
Total Assets = Current Assets + Fixed Assets
Total Assets = ₦2,000 + ₦4,000 = ₦6,000
Total Liabilities = Current Liabilities + Long Term Loan
Total Liabilities = ₦1,200 + ₦2,000 = ₦3,200
Using the accounting equation:
Capital = Total Assets - Total Liabilities
Capital = ₦6,000 - ₦3,200 = ₦2,800
Note: Drawings represent owner's withdrawals and don't affect the capital calculation using the accounting equation method.
Therefore, the capital of the business is ₦2,800.

To reconcile, we need to add back the dishonoured cheque amount to the cash book balance to reflect that this money was not actually received

The dishonoured cheque represents money that was recorded as received in the cash book but was actually not collected by the bank, so it increases the cash book balance during reconciliation to match the bank's records.

questions.text: Given: Capital ₦200,000, Liabilities ₦10,000, Total assets ₦210,000. If the business is purchased at a price including a goodwill of ₦20,000, what must have been the purchase price?

Net Worth = Total Assets - Total Liabilities
Net Worth = ₦210,000 - ₦10,000 = ₦200,000
(This also equals the Capital as shown: ₦200,000)
Step 2: Calculate the purchase price
Purchase Price = Net Worth + Goodwill
Purchase Price = ₦200,000 + ₦20,000 = ₦220,000

options: purchase consideration is greater than the net value
net assets is greater than the liabilitties
questions.explanation:
At par acquisition means the price paid for the business exactly equals the fair value of its net assets (i.e., assets minus liabilities).

In this case, no goodwill is recognized because there is neither a premium paid nor a discount received on the net assets.

Hence, the business is acquired “at par” when the purchase consideration equals the net asset value.

questions.text:
During the year ended 31st December 2001,
₦uju Enterprises paid rent as follows:
Jan. 20, ₦24 000 for a period of 4 months.
May. 16, ₦30 000 for a period of 5 months.
Oct. 15, ₦36 000 for a period of 6 months.

What is the overpaid portion of the rent?
questions.explanation:
Payment 1:
Jan 20 — ₦24,000 for 4 months → Jan 20 to May 19, 2001

All months are within 2001, so no overpayment.

Payment 2:
May 16 — ₦30,000 for 5 months → May 16 to Oct 15, 2001

All months are within 2001, so no overpayment.

Payment 3:
Oct 15 — ₦36,000 for 6 months → Oct 15, 2001 to Apr 14, 2002

From Oct 15 to Dec 31, 2001 → 2.5 months belong to 2001 (paid expense).

From Jan 1 to Apr 14, 2002 → 3.5 months belong to 2002 (prepaid).

Step 2 – Calculate prepaid portion from Payment 3
Cost per month = ₦36,000 ÷ 6 = ₦6,000/month

Prepaid = 3.5 months × ₦6,000 = ₦21,000
